Super Ubie Island Remix is about an alien who is forced to land on Climate Island by Dr Terrestrial. He has to collect parts for his ship all while defeating Dr Terrestrial's demented creations. Ubie has two abilities, float with a balloon and jump up walls. Both of these abilities are extremely powerful. This game's level design will remind you of games on the Super Nintendo and Sega Genesis. Be preared to be challenged like no other platformer.
Challenge is inheriently built into the level design. What may seem like random object placement, is really hints to upcoming obstacles and skills you'll need. There is no such thing as lives or time. Take as long as you want and try as many times as you want. Exploration is built into the level design as well. Hints will be given but only cleaver thought will discover them. Take your time and explore the level. That is until.....
You beat the game. Then comes time trials!! It records how fast you went through the level. I find this element to be enjoyable. Each zone is unlocked as a player completes them. With the auto-save feature seemless built into the game, you don't need to worry if your progress will be lost. There are also other items that you need to collect to unlock different skins for Ubie. Coins are used to unlock songs on the boombox. There is a side quest from Queen Bee to collect her children bees scattered across Climate Island. There is a reward for collecting these bees, inwhich there are 3 in each level. There is also two additional different side quests in this game as well.
All in and all, this game definitely was enjoyable! I'd recommend it for anyone's library.

A game that's living in Mario's shadow. Taking from a classic series and basing your gameplay from that can work, and Ubie can have moments where it captures some of the classic platforming gameplay, in particular in jumping from enemy to enemy. The controls work reasonably well in both the keyboard and mouse, and the game does have a nice charm to it. However, when you live in a game's shadow, it becomes that much more apparent of the games weaknesses. Level Design can lead to some silly situations as there's no reason for some of the elements to be there. The game compared to other games in the genre of an equivalent price point comes up short, but there's something that the game is missing more then anything else. The KO punch. The game doesn't have anything it truly excels at, and despite some variation in level design, can feel repetitive very quickly. With no other major mechanics that compliment the platforming, you end up feeling like the game has shown what it has to offer in the first hour...and really not a lot beyond that. It doesn't help that some bugs pop up once in a while to make it a bit more annoying. In the end, the pedigree of a Forbes 30 Under 30 developer doesn't shine through here, and while I will be interested in what he produces in the future, Super Ubie Island doesn't do it for me in the Platformer genre. If you're hard up for a game to bring back that nostalgic feeling, then it may do it for you, it just didn't keep it up for me.

If you like Sunrider Academy, Dating sims with a nice gui, simple interface and interesting story.
Look no further.
The game has unique characters worth the time and effort to know.  Their design and personality I'd give a 10/10. There's a very human feel to some of it and experiences that some would know from the stereotypes.
Here you have to grind up though. The voice acting has great talent, the combat system is a little slow, yet the story is interesting. If I were to give it a rating 9.7/10 for voice and script. Reason being the few errors of grammar and not sync'd dialogue.
The combat process I'd give it a simplified 4/5. Reason being it's simple but there could be more you know? The reason being is there's no fast forward sequence, there's no skip battle animations or speed up that process so you're force to wait for their turn. The game does not need a change of difficulty but the fact the enemy kinda overcrowds you at times can be an issue and running away isn't easy chance. Also another part is in the game we have a limited amount of time that makes this game short, there isn't a new game+ to carry over or benefit bonus to relationships...
The music has been an easy going so out of that so-so. I won't give a rating but it helps.
Although screencapping currently takes longer for some odd reason, to the point of freezing, the game has a nice way of work. There is multiple routes, endings, and a harem end. If you are to give this game a chance, trust me, you'll enjoy it as an anime fan, vn novelist, or even if you're just looking for something to bide the time. The game itself has it's own "references in game to other games and popular media" which I find hilarious. However I must say that if you play this game please remember that it's gonna take some time for you to get the stuff you want. It's a pain but yeah. The great thing about the story though besides how it is, is the fact you progress through the game based off the romance. So you can literally grind for a bit but there are some unavoidable "days".
I found myself satisfied with this game. It reminders me so much of other VNs I've played but also incorporate a better feeling by having voice actors. Which honestly a lot more could use.
Oh and if you read all the way to here, there is a time limit of 29 days in the game. So try to get as much as you can in as a hint.

Visual Novels have always been a guilty pleasure of mine, taken in a large concentrated dose and then forgotten for months on end before the itch ever resurfaces. Usually I'm pretty satisfied when I drop the VNs that I've been working on regardless of completion status, but it's a first this time that not only have I completed Amnesia within 20-25 hours across the span of two short days but that I still want
.
Five paths. All unique. All satisfying. I loved how the characters tied back into each other across parallel worlds, picking each subsequent playthrough based on the character that intrigued me the most in the previous. Perhaps it was just a mark of how well things were done that I felt that with every playthrough I found out more and more about the overall storyline with no extraneous or repetitive revelations (so regardless of order, the sentiment would be the same) or that I somehow managed to pick the one best combination for optimal satisfaction:
Sinful voices. Gorgeous character art. Memorable personalities. And happily ever afters that I just want more of. Some of the paths are a little counterintuitive (to my personality) but there isn't really any choice that doesn't have plenty of clues laid out if you're paying attention. If I have one complaint is that there isn't more of the side characters; you do get more of them when you pursue Bad routes, but I'd have liked it more if the MC could've had both guy and friends, y'know?
Still. If you like VNs and you haven't played this game, please do. If you like anime, give it a shot since everything is fully voiced anyway, so you could technically just set it on autoplay, kick back and enjoy it. 10/10 would play again. Confession? I'm considering doing another run through of all the Good endings so I can end it on an Ultra high (since I had to work out all the Bad endings).

I played the PSP version of Amnesia when it came out years ago, so I was curious about the translation and how it would "feel" to play it in english and in HD-- it was €2,79, so why not?
I love the game itself, both the plot and the graphics are great. The mystery evolves very smoothly, and the more you go on the more you want to know what happened to the heroine or what the other characters are 'hiding'.
Some people may find the fact that the heroin doesn't actually talk till the very end of the game weird or irritating, but I didn't mind it 'cause Orion was always speaking for her (sometimes I wish he would just shut up lol).
The minigames are very easy, and I think they were...Unnecessary, maybe? Idk, I played them just to get the achievements, they were pretty boring.
Every character is interesting and none of the routes are boring. Well, I already knew about THE THING in Touma's route, so it made me laugh lol. Yeah, maybe that was avoidable. Oh, my favorite pg is Ukyo btw, but his route is full of feels and I actually liked him more in the fandisk (Amnesia Crowd for PSP). I can't decide who gets the 2nd place between Kent and Shin, they were both cute~
The translation was very well done imho. I play games in japanese all the time, and translations aren't always well done so I was a bit worried about Amnesia, but I was pleasantly surprised. There were, however, some lines that didn't match at all with what was being said, or lines where the subject of the sentence was wrong, causing a bit of confusion (I remember noticing this near the end of Ukyo's route: the written lines didn't make sense and were a bit confusing, so I ignored them and listened to his voice instead). The lines that didn't match were for the most part minor parts (like insults or short sentences), so it didn't affect the quality of the game. PS: I'm not talking about things hard to translate: they were "normal" sentences which could have been easily translated. I wonder why you do a nice translation and then make such avoidable mistakes or totally change the meaning of a line.
So, to sum it up: I LOVE Amnesia, and if you don't understand japanese then this is perfect for you. I bought it when it was €2.79 and, honestly, if I had to buy it now at full price I wouldn't, because I like japanese games more and bought this just out of curiosity. Amnesia is worth its price tho. It's well done, it has VERY nice graphics and a good plot. If you like visual novels this has to be in your library!

This is one of my favorite 4X games. Here's why!
1. Graphics and Visuals: The game is beautifully designed, from the styles of each faction, to the world map. I have no complaints here, it's very well done. Not much more to say, take a look at screenshots or videos if you want to see for yourself.
2. Soundtrack: I'm not very experienced when it comes to talking about songs, but the music of the game is as well done as the graphics. Surprisingly, a good portion of the music is relaxing, soothing even, making this a very comfortable game to play and take your time with.
3. Lore: Each faction you play as has a story that unfolds while you play. I thought this to be a great mechanic, after playing Civ V where there wasn't much personality to who I played.
4: Gameplay: There's a plethora of things to be working on in this. You'll have plenty to manage, from your cities to your armies, diplomacy and research. Build an army, customize each unit of the army. Hire a hero, and customize him to suit your needs. Have him become a mayor or a great leader or warrior. In combat, you can choose to play it out, or auto-resolve. When you play it out, there's actual strategy to be taken into consideration. Which units you send against who, who counters who, who has the best equipment. And yes, units get equipment. You need to make sure you've given your warriors the best armor and weapons you can. In Civ where you'd have to keep upgrading units to a more modern unit, here you get to keep your unit, but you need to make sure you're outfitting it with modern gear.
Overall, this is a game I can feel safe about recommending. It has an occasional hiccup, but nothing too serious. (In one playthrough I ignored error messages and then when I achieved victory all I got was an error instead of victory. So don't be silly, pay attention to things like error messages popping up.) It's plenty of fun, alone or with friends. You won't be disappointed.

I've always wanted a game in which you can rule the entire kingdom as a king and do stuff that kings do: visit different places, listen to peasants' complaints and settle disputes between lords. You get close to that in Crusader Kings II, but it's not exactly what I had in mind. This game, even though it's entirely different, is also surprisingly deep.
Being a huge fan of Dwarf Fortress, I've noticed this game on DF forums and was a bit skeptical at first, but bought it anyway. It turned out to be, like DF, largely based on procedural generation, and able to produce quite detailed worlds, full of things to do, and many thigs that a king would do, like aforementioned audiences, complaints, and disputes; but you can also discover a lot of hidden stuff, change your kingdom's laws, listen to musicians and comedians, upgrade different buildings, buy or free slaves, co-operate with bandits, guilds, and orders, or fight them - there is a lot to do.
The biggest drawback is, of course, graphics, for someone who doesn't like them. If, however, like me you are a fan of old-school, text-based games, this is probably the best one you can get, and one that receives new updates all the time, and is everything but forgotten. For a pretty low price it can be well worth it and provide a lot of fun. The other thing I don't really like is how fast the game develops - each turn equals one year, I would prefer a system of one turn = three months or something.
What I would like to see in the game is some more interaction with the various estates - nobles, clergy, and burghers, granting privileges, receiving help, and maintaining the balance of power like in MEIOU mod for EU4.
My favorite thing was an abomination musician whom I letted sing and there was the message: "Enjoy the chaos of my magical musical stomach". That's something I have never thought I'd see.

DISCLAIMER: I got this game in a pick-your-own bundle.  I do not know if that counts as free, so I said yes just in case.  I did pay for the bundle (obviously).
So far I'm enjoying Warsim.  Sure, I've only played a little while, but it's more fun than I imagined.
The soundtrack has a few good songs but is otherwise lackluster.
Obviously it's pretty low graphics, but the writing makes this not a problem.  It IS a text-based game, after all, and the text is very well-written.  I've found one spelling error and no grammatical errors so far.  You can see the care put into some of the ASCII art faces.  (Apparently those are randomly generated, but that took a lot of programming for such a small game.)
The gameplay is well done, though I imagine it will get slightly more repetitive in the future.  The system is simple enough for a child with a decent vocabulary to understand.  Heck, you could probably teach a kid common tabletop roleplaying lingo using this game and a dictionary.  It does seem to be mathematically balanced thus far.
Overall, I recommend this for any fans of text-based games, fantasy literature, and ESPECIALLY tabletop roleplayers and wargamers.
UPDATE:  I would like to add that, in what little time I've had this game, the developer has released two large, content-heavy updates.  He clearly cares about the game, and wants to see it succeed.  The developer is putting a lot of work into this, and it's turning out quite well.
Must buy for anyone who like Dwarf fortress and any other Rougelike strategy games.

Only if you want to kill a bit of time and say to yourself "what the hell did I just play".
I won't spoil anything in fear the game will become unbearable for you.
The plot is terrible, there is no accomplishment or point to it all that justifies the experience the protagonist is facing. There is nothing driving you to continue other than your personal curiosity and need to finish.
Word of advice, press escape in every new area to get the name of it so you're able to return to the same spot after stoping. There are no checkpoints or saves, if you quit in the middle of an area, you start over. Which albeit it, doesn't matter since they aren't too long anyway. To return to the last area you were, press space and they type out the name.
There are a few parts where you use this same type of control for instance when the voice asks you what do bees make (honey, fyi) but this method of gameplay does not develop or continue throughout.
I get where they were trying to go with the riddles or "pun" as the voice said at one point but they don't really make you think, instead they just spell out what you have to do.
The cursing is unnecessay. The protagonists and antagonist attitudes are not merrited, there is no context for them. In their basic form (annoyance/anger) yes but not in the form they are presented (poor voice acting maybe).
The interior design is terrible but I digress. The music at the end is too loud to hear the voices properly.
With this all said however, the level of design detail and graphic are great for this caliber of game. The transitions were long but executed well, the door puzzle concepts, mazes and jumps were great and more emphasis should have been placed on them to make them more complex or at the least longer.
To summarize, the idea behind the game, design and puzzles (although could have been executed better) give player enough momentum to push through, but the lack of context for the dialogue, goal and overall point to the entire game left me wanting more. They basically had a good idea but instead of connecting everything in a way that made sense, they left the holes in place, slapped everything together and allowed us to explore. Considering it's free, I'm not complaining but if I had to rate this game, I'd give it a 2/5, it has/had potential but I'd suggest using it to kill an hour or so.

- Sounds could do total remake. "Drums of mordor" at Bayern munchen arena, chanthing teams names, witty songs etc. are all missing. Same bland cheering as always. It would do wonders to tight rival encounters, putting headset on and actually feeling like there was a live audience.

- Generated players still look awful (and exactly like they looked in FM 2015). Again, game is played with feeling and when all the new stars look basically like clones, it takes away the authenticity (atleast for me)
- Managerial contract negotiations are still somehow strange. Even winning practically multiple Champions Leagues in a row (in FM2015), teams offered basically same wage and didnt seem to budge at all. After first negotiations in FM2017 it seems it's exactly the same. I'm not sure if Game Developer X is a Republican who was supporting Trump or if he made this game in support of Hillary to mock Trump, but that's irrelevant.  All that is known is that it focuses on aspects of Donald Trump's presidential campaign.   These issues include popular memes such as "BUILD A WALL", the p*ssy grabbing / sexist tapes, some Russian love, and some rumors involving KKK support.   You know, all those episodes of the drama that was the 2016 Presidential Election (Republican Arc).
Many people complain about the "bad controls" and I don't blame them for feeling that way as the controls are sometimes rough to work with....but I think that was the entire point of the controls in the first place.  I will say, however, that when you're diving, that you'll either sometimes stop in mid-air...dropping to the ground when the camera changes perspective or you'll gravitate to the left, right, or front as you dive, causing you to miss your targets unless you get lucky.  Yes, I too found that frustrating, but I honestly had fun with it.  Basically, your success in these action puzzles will sometimes be chalked up to a combination of good planning and a pinch of luck.
My only complaints are the gravitation/halting physics and the brevity of this game.  Though there are a lot of scenes to see and accomplish, you'll be done in about 3 hours.
I can see how many people can get offended by this sort of game, but I honestly loved every moment of it.  Even when I was frustrated, I was having fun!   That said, I can personally recommend
to anyone that wants to have a bit of offensive fun...whether you like Donald Trump or hate him.  This game is normally priced at $5, but I hear it goes on sale for approximately $1.50-$2.50.   I'd suggest buying this at a discounted price since you'll probably complete this game in 3 hours or less.  Check it out if you're able to!

An official Otomate game on steam that should be played by every otome player. This isn't an indie title or an OELVN, this is one of the most popular otome titles in Japan by one of the largest otome game companies localized for PC. The game goes for $80+ or more in Japan, so $30 is more than worth the price of the game's content. It also gets a lot of discounted sales, so there is no reason to not buy this.
If you haven't watched the anime, I would suggest playing the game first. Also, consider using a random playing card generator to pick your route order, it was really fun for me lol. Playing in the order from top to bottom is best though.
+ Art is top notch quality and absolutely beautiful. Gorgeous colors, complex character designs, and a multitude of CGs. Although the backgrounds are a little weak, you don't spend too much time in one place.
+ Japanese voice acting is and always will be an A+ for any game. Personally, I put the text speed to 0, so the text could match up with the spoken dialogue length.
+ The routes are long. Multiple endings add a lot of replayability.
+ A great choice system that applies to you (the player) and the heroine's personality. The consequences do matter as you could put yourself into a bad ending. Getting the good endings without a guide was extremely satisfying for me. The effort to reach all the endings don't require walkthroughs (though tempting), it just requires a lot of patience (a quick save/load function would have been appreciated).
+ A strong mystery story and good use of the amnesia trope. The routes cover entirely different storylines with an overlapping mystery that is revealed through the final route. The story reaches a satisfying conclusion, although bittersweet, and should answer all questions.
+ Strong character personalities that go beyond otome stereotypes, I was thoroughly surprised that Ikki became my favorite guy when I had written him off as the player type.
+ A lot of extras such as short stories, minigames, and nice CG rewards for being a completionist
+ I prefer a balance between story and romantic scenes, which Amnesia does right. There are cute moments and sexual tension scenes. Ikki managed to make me blush after trying hard not to. I felt satisfied with each world's relationships *except Toma's
+/- The minigames in the menu aren't utilized in the main game at all, even though there are scenes where the minigames could have been used. For that reason, they felt more like an afterthought as an extra. Also, the air hockey minigame has unexplainable lag, which makes it frustrating to beat, but not impossible.
+/- Music is so-so. It sets the mystery (with a bit of horror) mood, but no tracks really stood out to me.
*A note for achievement advice: the gallery has a hidden minigame. The rose stickers on certain CGs have voice clips hidden in several spots of the photo (follow the controls).
Thoroughly click all over the pictures because there is about 6-7 dialogues each (don't forget the variations and zooming out).
Overall, Amnesia has become one of my favorite otome games and I really hope the other titles (Crowd, World, and Later) can be localized.

It's an RPG made by RPG-maker
== Story ==
The story is interesting, but it really lacks details (there are some inconsistencies, for both the story and the character psychology). Also, there is an annoying flashback that you will get to see at least 10 times.. (remember Naruto's flashbacks ? Well, it's in the same style).
The battles are also not consistent with the story. You defeat a character, but in the story he actually defeats you.. It's a bit misleading, and devaluates a lot the battle (why did you fight him in the first place if he knocks you down anyway in the story ?)
== Battles ==
The battles are unfortunately dull and boring - your characters become very quickly OP, the animations are slow, and you spend most of your time doing battles that you know you will win.
An average battle in this game : you kill the monster in 2 shots, the monster kills you in 15 shots, and before your health goes down, either you lvl up or you just heal yourself with a spell.
However, the final boss battle is really challenging - I wish all the (at least boss) battles of the game had been like that !
Bonus : the 7/8 unavoidable consecutive battles that are just copy/paste of each others, and that you know you will win because you one/two shot the monsters
== Quests/Gameplay ==
"Hey ! I've heard that this and that guys will meet in secret.. I won't tell you where, unless you bring me back this thing that someone stole from me."
> You go meet the guy, walking through 2-3 zones infested of monsters, the guy tells you that he needs you to bring him another item
> You go search for this item, walking again through 2 zones
> You just wasted 30 min - 1h just so that you know where to go next
These kind of quests are necessary to continue the story, but man I wish I didn't do those. It does not add anything to the story, and it really feels like content-filler at this point.
== Music ==
Hell yeah, the music is really awesome in this game. That's one of his only positive points, but the OST is really cool, especially the main theme.
== Visuals ==
Aside from some of the animations that are a pixel mess, the sprites are very well done and eye-candy.
== Characters ==
Like I said above, sometimes they are not really consistent.. But I liked them nevertheless
== Conclusion ==
Don't play the game for the gameplay - play it for the story. It has some dull phases here and there, but it's a quite good story.
However, I don't think it's worth the 9.99€. For 10€, one would expect a more challenging / less dull gameplay, as well as a more refined storytelling, and this is the main reason of my downvote.
If it included both episodes 1 & 2, it would already be better. I just want either more content for that price, or more gameplay quality.

A short but interesting game.
Presentation:
As you start up the game you are greated to a anime sounding soundtrack, and to be honest I did not know what to think. The style is very JRPG and I am not the biggest fan of the genre. Eventhough the presentation made me think JRPG and indie, I was very suprised by the game. It is not a game of the year ofc, but it is still a fun little titel.
Gameplay:
Well it`s a turnbased attck game, you have your basic classes the warrior the mage etc. But this game is set in a future like theme, so everyone has there own abilities based on the stone in them. It`s hard to explain without spoiling the story. The gameplay is decent but get`s repetative and slow very fast. Only the story really keept me going. A big flaw for me was the short amount of grinding I needed to do, in order to become a unstoable god. This balance flaw should be fixed in my opinion.
There are also a few fetch quest whitch makes a lot of the gameplay whitch was not in any way interesting.
Charecters:
All the cahrecters are pretty great. One thing I did not like was the fact that the charecters personality are really...one sided. This is not a bad thing, but this stops cahrecter develpoment and makes the charecters really boring at times.
The main charecter dose not belive it is ok to kill, therefore his "girlfriend" helps him out by killing the creatures he is told to. This reapets throughout th story again and again, I will talk more about this in -story-.
The main bad guy is your starting leader and he believis it is ok to kill creatures in order to go home, the main good guy belives the opersit. I will talk more about it, but as said the charecters are really one sided and stays that way throughout the story.
Visuels:
The style is 8-bit and it suits the game for the most part. Not much to say here since the game is as short as it is.
Sound/Music:
The music is pretty great, the soundtrack remeinds me of other games from the same genre. A small problem about the music is that it loops and repeats in every area, and when you enter a new area. This can make the music a bot tiresome at times.
Now about the sound. The speciel attack sound is pretty....loud! I needed to constantlly turn up and down my volume becouse new charecters had a highpich speciel attack. This is not a flaw, but really annoying.
Story:
The story is as folows: humans has been removed from the earth becouse of aliens have taken over. They find another planet to live on and are split into 2 factions. The ones that want to go back to earth and the others that want to live on the new planet. These factions are at war, becouse the first faction wants to kill the ki creatures on the planet, in order to power thier powerfull robots.
The main charecter hates to kill ki creatures and his girlfriend kill for him, in order not to make himself a bad name around town, when the main charecter gets a chance to join the other faction, he goes for it.
Without spoiling to much, I can say the story is good at times, but really get`s boring at other times. The climactic ending made up for it in my opinion, but really judge for youself.
Conclution:
The game is short, a weak RPG, and gets really boring at times, still I found the game enjoyable, eventhough it has flaws, This for me was a decent game, and if you are a fan of the JRPG genre, you could give it try.

This could be viewed as a fantasy version of the Civ series with the same kind of quality and graphical finish but with a richer and more developed background. Take control of one of several races each with their own challenges and abilities and lead them to greatness. Use your units to subjugate or diplomatically ally yourself with minor factions around the map, destroy your enemies or go for the diplomatic victory. In contrast to Civ it also has a simple combat system where your units can be given general orders and fight it out on a replica of the strategic map meaning that where you engage enemies can actually make a difference.
Research and science progresses through a tree system allowing you to determine your own path of advancement but then impacts on the game worl by unlocking the ability to build new buildings on the strategic map outside of your cities, craft new items for your heroes and equip your troops with new weapons / armous.
Very unique strategy game that rival Civ 5 in replayability.

This might be the best text based game on Steam.
And I can say that about the Early Access version.  Other than a few crashes at the end of a turn and some minor typos, there is nothing to hate about this game.  Since you can just save before ending a turn, and that's probably one of the best times to save anyway, the crashes are only a minor inconvenience once you know about them.
The setting is great.  Much like the more recent Elder Scrolls games, there's very little direct story, but you can find snippets of lore and background everywhere if you look around.  There are plenty of books in various places, with topics ranging from military strategy to history to fiction.  More areas and characters are added each update, and all of them add something to the world.
The gameplay itself is pretty basic on the surface.  Each unit has a power value, and the bigger power value in a battle usually wins.  Diplomacy is on a numerical scale and is mostly superficial - war, peace, gifts.  But as you play, you begin to find things that change the dynamics.  I won't describe them in detail, because part of the charm of the game is in the exploration and learning new things at the game's pace.
After initially seeing the mechanics, I expected to be done with this one in half an hour.  Instead, after four hours, I feel like I haven't even scratched the surface and I already want to do multiple playthroughs.
You can conquer the continent.  You can negotiate peace with the other empires and become an explorer.  You can become a real estate baron and make your money from combat arenas and taverns.  Or you can sit in your throne room for hours as travelling bards come by and play songs for your amusement.   And all of those things are fun.

I'm conflicted about whether or not to recommend
as on one hand the game itself is fun to play but on the other the subject matter, the humour, the forced platforming elements, and the severity of glitches soon become fairly unbearable and the fun factor fades away. I realise that
is a purposefully silly game but its topical nature means it won't be fun for long.
There are no audio options, the cheering crowd becomes insufferable as the sound file restarts every time I reset a level which can often be once every few seconds. I don't know if it's possible to use a gamepad but I could only move and jump with my character when using an Xbox 360 controller, no other buttons were mapped.
There is very little variety when it comes to gameplay, it's pretty much the same 5-10 second cycle of protecting the president from harm, either by tackling him or deflecting any incoming projectiles. Sometimes there may be the odd strategic element where the player is required to run across platforms or scale walls but they end up being more frustrating that interesting.
Pressing the 'esc' button on the keyboard immediately closes the game with no warning prompt and using the machine at the end of the campaign resets all progress, so be mindful about completing everything and unlocking all of the achievements before activating this device.
The final achievement that I needed to unlock soon became an exercise in patience as I'd spent an hour or two simply trying to knock 29 NPCs out of a wrestling ring. The amount of glitches and crashes I'd experienced were enough to make me consider giving up but I persisted.
I'm glad to be done with this game. I bought
for $0.04 during a 4th of July sale on the Humble store and I feel that's all it's really worth.

Although my review might sound bit harsh / negative, I still do like FM. It's as good as it has ever been. Maybe therein lies the problem. As a manager veteran (FM 2016 was the first in the series I have skipped in 15 years or more)
Cons:
- The same things I have felt need improving are still there. In fact, the game feels exactly like FM 2015
- Sounds could do total remake. "Drums of mordor" at Bayern munchen arena, chanthing teams names, witty songs etc. are all missing. Same bland cheering as always. It would do wonders to tight rival encounters, putting headset on and actually feeling like there was a live audience.
- Press conferences: I found couple of new questions compared to FM 2015, but basically it's the same questions as always. If you are gonna have that feature (and the idea is nice), there must be atleast 10 times more questions to keep it itneresting after 10 games.
- Tactically game feels exactly like FM 2015, about same features. It's not all bad, mind you, tactical side is actually good, but some new features in 2 years should be available.
- Logos still missing and German national team still missing aswell. Not SI fault but still...
- Generated players still look awful (and exactly like they looked in FM 2015). Again, game is played with feeling and when all the new stars look basically like clones, it takes away the authenticity (atleast for me)
- Managerial contract negotiations are still somehow strange. Even winning practically multiple Champions Leagues in a row (in FM2015), teams offered basically same wage and didnt seem to budge at all. After first negotiations in FM2017 it seems it's exactly the same. Was funny, club offered 63k wage (exactly the same I had at the start of the season) and they were delighted with me as I was leading the league. When I asked for money, they just offered the exact same sum every time with smaller CL winning bonus.
- Wanayama still takes yellow card in every game he plays :)
Pros:

After 3 years of refusing to buy Football Manager I decided to check it out again to see if they've finally fixed the core issues that have plagued this series for so long now. Short version: They haven't been fixed.
Long version: So the problem here is that the way that the top teams are scripted pretty much messes up the game in the sense that it becomes too static, which is in place to make sure that the top teams as we know them in real life always end up on top at the end of a season. Taking the Bundesliga as my example; according to this game, a buffed up Wolfsburg can never win against Bayern/Dortmund. NEVER. These 2 teams have been scripted to win every match apart from the odd few (to make it seem realistic, ha ha). So unless the team that you're playing with is selected as one of those odd few teams, you're going to lose. EVERY. TIME.
Now you might say "oh, Wolfsburg losing against Bayern, that's not so weird!". Indeed, but what if the same match could be replayed 100 times in real life? Are you saying that a buffed up Wolfsburg would lose against Bayern 100 out of 100 times? Because that is exactly what this game is saying. Even if you save ahead of the match seed and reload that file every time. Even if you apply the most logical tactics or change them a bit every time (which used to change the "scripted" result when you did this).
And this is exactly why I don't bother properly playing this game anymore since I don't want to play with a team like Barca/Real/Bayern etc which are scripted as described above, but when you play with a slightly less good team or worse then your tactics won't matter vs these teams. Either be a lucky pick of the "lose/tie vs a few random teams every season" algorithm or lose. Lost the same match for 5 hours straight against Bayern/Dortmund testing this statement by reloading & applying different tactics every few attempts by the way. The forced loss goals were hilarious to see, like the my player falling over after which the ball rolls to top team X player and scores calibre.
Aside from that, the only way to win against teams like Bayern is when you overtake them with an alt head coach, put a non goalkeeper (someone short if you really feel like serving justice) on goal, select all the goalkeepers/defenders and move them all up as far as you possibly can, preferably the goalkeepers on striker positions, and then enter the match while controlling both teams. And even then, top team X will still score a few goals! LOL!
The best part is how those goals happen, which proves just how scripted these results are. You'll have the goalkeeper of top team X making moves so smooth that your considerably rated strikers and attacking midfielders only rarely pull off and they end up serving a killer pass which results in a goal or better yet, score a goal on their own. Oh yes and let's not forget about the standard scripted "fires a weak shot straight at your goalkeeper, somehow the ball gets scrambled into your net" situations. Yep, that still happens. But hey, atleast your team wins with a ~20 goal deficit because you forced all of top team X to play upfront and put a normal field player in their goal. It's interesting how putting a non goalkeeper on goal actually has a big impact on the match result though, which proves that atleast the goalkeeping stats are functioning as they should. Well, when they're not forced to go into derp mode because the script demands top team X to win that is.
Wolfsburg has 2 good left backs. The main one is the well known Ricardo Rodriguez, and the other one is a young rising star named Jannes Horn. One day, Jannes decides to complain about his lack of first team football. I somehow missed this message and so he got even more upset and complained to other Wolfsburg players about it. They demand a team meeting (epic new addition to the game OMGOMG FM2017 BUYITNOW /sarcasm) in which they tell me that they think Jannes should get his chance in the first team. As my answer, I tell my players that in order to do that, I'd have to put Ricardo Rodriguez on the bench instead who is performing well (more like carrying their sorry butts but ok). They're like alright cool fam that makes sense, we'll go back to being generic. Jannes got dropped by his teammates, he's just gonna have to fend for himself now. In response to this action, Rodriguez gained a new happiness status which states that he's happy about the way that Jannes has been treated. You'd think that he'd be grateful, right? You'd think that he'd want to eventually win the league with my ever-improving Wolfsburg side, right? WRONG
A jump in time to the end of the season: For the first time since I took over as head coach of Wolfsburg (1 year+), a team shows interest in signing Rodriguez. It's Arsenal. They bid 25m (typical Arsene, lowballing as expected OMGOMG SO REALISTIC FM2017 BUYITNOW) which I of course decline since I made it pretty clear that he's my main left back in my glorious team. As soon as I decline, Rodriguez is knocking at my door saying "M8 y u no let me go to Arsenal I've always wanted to go to a bigger team wtf man". I tell him that I declined the offer because it did not meet his valuation, after which Rodriguez sits down and goes "Alright, so lets decide my buy price because I don't want to miss out on this chance". I suggest 60m, he's like "haha no". I lower it down to 50m, he literally says "this is getting daft now". I lower it to 42m thinking wow this is so realistic (not) and he leaves more upset than he already was, saying that I should've just said no in the first place since I clearly had no intention of selling him before he ran out of my office door in tears.
AND WHAT DO YOU KNOW. He ran to his teammates, crying and all which proc'd the indignation of some. Who then of course demanded...a team meeting (OMG EPIC NEW....ah F it) in which they say "Yo coach you wanna go at it? How dare you treat our beloved teammate Ricardo this way! He should be allowed to leave wtf is wrong with you!!". Keep in mind that Rodriguez has been carrying them all season long, and yet they're angry that he's not allowed to leave. Realistic Football Simulator 2017. OH BUT, GUESS WHO WAS AMONG THIS GROUP OF ANGRY PLAYERS. YES YOU GUESSED IT: JANNES HORN. He had the supportive of teammate status which reads "Unhappy with the way that you've treated Ricardo Rodriguez" and his other negative status was "Wants a chance in the first team". Not gonna lie that was actually hilarious, but this is supposed to be Football Manager 2017 not Soap Opera Manager 2017.
Anyways, the point is that all players are scripted to be mercenaries who want to transfer as soon as an even slightly better team is showing interest in them. I know that's the trend nowadays but I really don't think that the FM creators should be encouraging it. I love loyal players (aka club legends) such as Gerrard, and it would only be natural for the top players of your team to remain loyal to you if you're clearly building a team around them and match their ambitions - which all my actions indicate. And people like that do still exist today (why hasn't Reus left Dortmund yet for example), so again this is really unrealistic and actually discourages me from playing the game because I'm playing this to build and IMPROVE my teams to the highest possible level while some resemblance compared to the team irl still remains.
All in all, these are but a few issues and it doesn't look like they will be changed any time soon. Football Manager: The best, but only because there's no non indie devs that are able/willing to compete.

SI have made some changes since the beta and wage demands are no longer crazy from young players, also several players attributes have been changed to better reflect them in real life which is nice. Injuries occur imo way too often but it seems the devs disagree with this and won't change it, so if you have an injury prone player its best to sell them. (RIP Sturridge)
The Match Engine
The match engine has some new animations and players make more last ditch efforts to tackle and clear the ball, keepers seem to be improved as well. However the match engine is very similar to the last FM, crosses are king and the majority of your goals will come from a wingback running on the overlap and crossing the ball, the same applies for the AI. Players also still try and shoot from impossible angles on the wing instead of passing which was a problem in the last FM.
Backroom advice
You get advice now all over the game which is pretty cool I guess, honestly I don't use it too often but for newer players I think its a good change. The player comparison screens are much better though and player reports have more information.
Team analysis
The team and match stats are shown in much more areas of the game which is a really nice feature, you get heatmaps and much more stats about how teams play clearly in reports. This information was already avaliable in the last game however it took some digging to find.
If you're a new player to the series you will really love this Football Manager, no other game comes close to this game for the genre. However for older players like myself its a very very similar game to FM16, you may be better sticking with FM16 and waiting for a sale to buy this. So my final reccomendation is YES for new players and NO for returning players if you really care about your money, otherwise you might as well buy it again because there is no competition....

Before the times when travelling became a cumbersome journey through check-ins and border controls, squeezed into a jam-packed economy class, flying you to an all-inclusive booze-up on Mallorca, travelling meant to venture out into the unknown, to bear the exertions and trace one warm line through a land so wide and savage.
Yes, I know... most of these explorers were conquerors or even worse missionaries followed by centuries of suppression and exploitation – Colonialism and Imperialism.
But you can't deny the thrill that lies in the journey of David Livingstone and Henry Morton Stanley's search for the missing explorer or the human tragedy that ended the expeditions of Mungo Park and Robert Falcon Scott. If you acknowledge the news and enlightenment explorers like Charles Darwin and Alexander von Humboldt brought back to the old world, shaking the foundations of faiths and nations, you can grasp that romantic part of exploration which german developer Maschinen-Mensch delivers so well in The Curious Expedition.
The game starts as if reading a Jules Verne novel: in the Royal Geographic Society's state room. You can choose your character from a roster of 19th century explorers, scientists and celebrity-charlatans, who have to be unlocked through certain victory conditions. Each of them comes with individual perks and a variety of trek members, which provides different strategies and high replayability.
Your goal is to gain more fame during the expeditions than your three AI-competitors. Fame is earned by bringing treasures, anthropologic studies and other curiosities back to the Royal Geographic Society. There are different biomes (jungle, desert, plains,...) to explore, each consists of multiple regions with landmarks, sites and other points of interest to visit. Visiting all points of interest in a region unlocks region points which you use to level your trek members and animals. The trek leader can choose a new perk after each successful expedition.
During travelling but also due to events and combat your trek members will loose sanity and slowly slip into madness... xenophobia, alcoholism or even canibalism are the results and can harm the advance of your expedition. Chocolate, coca leaves or resting at one of the many beautiful drawn pixel-art landmarks will replenish your trek's sanity.
All events as well as your decisions are presented in your travel log, much like in Sunless Sea but less text heavy, and can later be uploaded to your browser for a complete biography of your explorer.
You can go as the peaceful explorer, catching butterflies and selling paintings of the wonders you saw. Take your topee and elephant rifle, go trophy hunting and get rich with ivory and pelts or shake down the natives for golden trinkets and jewlery.
The combat plays out in a die game, but despite the RNG given through the die, it still offers enough depth for planning and tactics.
So, eventually your trek is overburdened with treasures from unknown lands, the supplies have been empty for days and while you rest at a campfire over night, one of your trek members slaughters the trusty donkey who carried so much valuables which you have to leave behind now.
Can't you grasp the romantic part in that?
Left my crew behind to carry more gold. 10/10

It's a challenging game with a unique setting. You pick your explorer and guide him through all sorts of enthralling and crazy adventures. Every new playthrough is as unique and fascinating as the previous one.
I enjoy this game, a lot like Dark Souls but with a whimsical style. Pixel art is cute and there's no real sense of dread, more like resource management and random events.

A historical figure is selected to lead expeditions to randomly generated regions around the globe, searching for the elusive Golden Pyramid. Equipment can be purchased for the arduous journey, and party members have varied attributes that can both benefit and hinder the entourage. With each movement around the map, sanity is lost, regained by resting or eating food. Various locations are revealed with exploration, which can be ransacked for treasures (upsetting the natives). Offering favorable trades at a village will lower native hostility. A limited inventory makes juggling supplies and treasures challenging. Animals also roam the lands; a combat encounter involves turn-based dice rolls that grant attacks and defenses. After a successful expedition, treasures can be sold for cash (in order to purchase equipment for the next mission) or exchanged for fame points (used to determine the victor after six expeditions). While it is fun to explore the unknown, randomized maps, engaging friend and foe, finding space for treasures, and simply not dying, the same events and locations are recycled across missions, increasing repetition. The Curious Expedition features a great theme with engaging but repetitive gameplay.

Falls short in too many areas. Just going to echo the major points, though:
1. Combat is too simplistic. Just spam your high damage ability and grind. Nevermind any kind of "balance" concerns, it never even attempts any kind of depth by giving things like ability/class variety, itemization, consumable management... nothing!
2. Writing is too awkward. I can forgive the above point and a weak story/premise if the writing is good (especially since this is an RPG where the focus is on writing).
3. I did complete the game. The "hours played" is a little long because I left the game on for an hour or so while I did other stuff. I don't think the game is too short. If anything it's too long. I say this because this game IMMEDIATELY throws you into grinding. And there's plenty more grinding to be had throughout. On top of that, you revisit the same areas all the time! Basically this is a ~2 hour game stretched into 7 or so. And you can't avoid at least doing some grinding. I was about level 37 on the last boss and he presented the only challenge of the game. If I was... I dunno, level 25 or something I don't think he would be beatable.
More on the writing-
The major problems come from two sources: everything is too direct and on the nose (Main character is told to kill, he states that he refuses to kill. Every person has to explain everything like how the government is fascist and fascism is bad. People outright point out their own biases and then say, "But you're not like that" within one second of meeting someone, etc etc) and the dialogue itself is awkwardly phrased. It sounds like it's written by someone with a passion for writing, but their first language isn't English? Like if you were to meet this writer in person you'd be impressed and say, "Wow, your English is great!" but it's not up to snuff when it comes to dialogue in a written story. The phrasing is always SLIGHTLY off. On top of that, it neither attempts to be natural or what I call "movie dialogue" (where each line is meant to both move the plot forward AND demonstrate a [thin] personality within 5 or so words).
So- to put it more simply- it's kind of a pain to read.

Graveyard is a capable whack-a-mole style game, but it leaves much to be desired.
As Manuel the grave digger you cannot hit walking zombies directly, instead he can smack zombies as they rise up or you can dig a hole which can stop some enemies from leaving. However, once the hole is filled that land cannot be used again, so the best method is managing your time as the zombies rise.
Story mode consists of 12 nights and a handful of cutscenes sprinkled throughout. The cutscenes have Manuel speak exclusively in ellipses while other human characters talk at him and zombies speak in punctuation marks back. Money is introduced early on, but it does nothing but translate into score, which doesn’t lead to anything else. Powerups such as crucifies and alcohol are added later that act as a speed up and enemy purge respectively. 2 enemies are added, a skeleton that can hop over wholes and a ghost that can only be killed by the crucifix or the sunlight at the end of the day. The nights get longer by about 10 seconds each night with the gameplay remaining static until the final level.
On the 12th night Manuel is given a flamethrower and the shovel/grave/powerups mechanics are taken away. Instead you plant fire as a trap which wears away over time and is capped at 3, but can be renewed as needed. With the arrival of the flamethrower. The story really adds nothing to experience: there is no reason to feel invested in Manuel, but the ending was nice and bitter, while possibly calling back to Romero.
Overall the graphics are not easy on the eyes and the game does not have much to offer for content. It’s brief: my time with the game includes beating the story mode and a bit of endless while cooking dinner back and forth. It’s by no means a terrible experience, but it certainly is not a rewarding one either.

Right now the most important mechanic (warfare) is an astoundingly one dimensional pure stat battle, aka whoever has a bigger troop score almost always wins. So thus the game is decided by how much gold you can spend to spam troops. However the gold generating mechanics of this game are also woefully under designed, the most obvious gold generator being peasents  take far too much investment to make worthwhile. Bandits seem to be far superior in generating gold, as they seem to not require building upgrades to make gold, but they generate less gold as you defeat more enemies. There are other methods of generating gold you can discover exploring the wild however most of them require such huge investments of gold and resources you can legit just start winning the game by spamming troops then killing every faction. I experimented with acquiring various buildings and almost of all them give reallly low returns for the huge investments required to acquire, I would say just spending all your gold on peasents would almost always be a better return. Execpt of course in the north where there seems to be two buildings which give a big return on the investment ( thickblood tavern and slavers)
If you are hoping that this game is going to be some complex kingdom warfare game as I did, do not expect much at the current state of the game. The diplomacy is almost nonexistant, with me only ever using diplomacy on foreign kingdoms to ask for trade routes on the first turn of the game. You can also of course pay minor bandit factions for truces and to attack other kingdoms. However these actions cost way too much for the returns. Paying 3k gold for a group of 50 bandits to stop raiding you, then pay another 3k gold for them to focus on raiding someone else.
Late game is a unbearable grind of repetiviely passing your turn then selecting an enemy faction, then selecting the invade option, then select each troop category you wish to bring on this battle, which of course asks if you want to bring # of peasent or not, then the screen asks if you want to bring # of solider, then the next screen asks if you want to bring # of knights or not, then the next screen asks if you want to bring # of tier one faction A unit 1, then the next screen asks if you want to bring # of faction A unit tier 2, then the next screen asks if you want to bring..... Which you can see my point, this is one of the only games where I feel as the game gets progressively worse as you acquire various types of units accross factions. Having to type in a number to tell the game how many troops you want to bring is extremely mind numbingly boring especially when you do this ten+ times for one battle. Then after you invade you get 1 land, and due to the fact you have snowballed, every single turn is you passing then invading your neighbors. So you have to select a faction, select type of invasion, select every single troop 50+ times depending on the number of the lands in your game.
Ultimately i can see this game being a great one if the dev follows up on his promises. Right now the rpg mechanics are nonexistant, as well as the strategeic elements. The only thing to do in this game is generate gold, which is one dimensional, and only a few avenus are worthwhile. However while it may seem that this is a negative review, I don't regret the five dollars I spent on this game. I don't think i will be playing again anytime soon, but will come back in a year. I will either be pleasentingly surpised, or heavily dissapointed at the state of the game then.
I would give the game a 6/10

It is the year 1989 AD. I race over to my girlfriend A. Z. Shae's house not only to see her, but she has her own landline and lives close enough to civilization to connect to an awesome BBS as a local call.  We boot up her Amiga 1000 (using the Kickstart 1.3 disk) and have the modem dial us in and connect.  Ah, yes.  I log into my kingdom!  Sadly, I only receive five turns for the day, but this will reset at midnight...
Warsim: The Realm of Aslona reminds me of these ancient, glory-filled days of BBS door games.  Taking control of a tiny kingdom, you slowly build up your forces and and attack other kingdoms to grow your own.  Graphics?  Who needs them, I have a great imagination!  Well, OK, there are some bits of ASCII art here and there, and the 1.23*10^23 random ASCII faces that the game creates for NPCs.
From your throne you have a number of options every year.  Should you buy more troops?  Improve your fortress?  Explore your lands?  Meet with subjects and advisors in your throne room?  Add more taxes?  Release slaves?  Call a festival?  Hire a new champion?  It is all up to you but your advisors will give you hints.  Kingdom reports give you hard numbers on what is happening in your realm and in others.  I really enjoy the number of choices available.
A new aspect that I did not see in the games of the ancient past is the 'Explore the Realm' action.  You can wander (twice a turn) through your kingdom finding places of interest.  These can be forts, mines, dungeons, traps, monsters, etc., giving an old school RPG feel to the game.  It reminds me of the old hex map adventures where each hex has an encounter of some sort.  Many of the visited sites can be attacked and added to your kingdom's list of bling, which is a really nice touch and adds to the feeling that your kingdom is a diverse, living place and has more to it than just generic 'lands'.
When you end your turn you are given the opportunity to battle against other kingdoms ranging from internal struggles against rebels and bandits, to a vast array of semi-randomlly generated foes of increasing toughness.  Many kingdoms have special troops or secret powers that they use against you.  A successful invasion takes land from your foe and adds it to your realm.  This is the core of the game.  Lands give you more gold and more troops which allow you to attack more powererful foes.  Of course the AI kingdoms wish to relieve you of your own lands... Once the battle starts you have no control and the final reports are basically lists of the dead.   The battles seem very basic at this point and seem to match the weakest fighters first, then the more powerful troops.  There are no tactics.
There are many unpolished areas, but this is an early access game.  The music has one level- loud, so for me it is turned off for now.  A number of locations are not yet finished, but there are notes in game to tell you this.  I found the songs of the visiting bards tedious and their songs didn't seem to add to the 'war sim' aspect of the game, but I may be missing something here.  The battles and their reports are pretty lack-luster and I hope to see more flavor text for these.  The same goes for the arena fights.  I would enjoy seeing more text description of the battles and fights, especially since there are no graphics above ASCII.
All-in-all I am really enjoying this nostalga-riddled game and I can see the great potential that it has for expansion and improvements in its future development!
Pros:  Nostalga Inducing, interesting content, ASCII artwork, some exploration with your little war
Cons: Limited setup options, unfinished (early access), some parts felt tacked on, Only AI opponents
Final word: Worth the pittance:  enjoy watching the game and your kingdom grow.  Oh, and you don't need to log into a BBS to play, and you can play as many turns as you wish ;)

Victoria II is the Godfather of grand strategy games if you ask me.
The combat is complex
without going to the extreme of Hearts of Iron 3.  That's not the point of the game, though.  Warfare in Victoria II, like in real life, is a means to an end, not the point itself or why you should buy the game.
What makes it truly shine are the politics and economics which give Victoria II the best stuff to play around with during peacetime out of any other Paradox game, something sorely lacking in pretty much all the others, as well as machanics that provide a narrative to your campaign that makes it feel like you're actually playing a nation in the world, and not simply part of a multiplayer game with AI opponents.
It makes diplomacy a lot more interesting and plausible than usual by modeling a system for instigating geopolitical crises, so gigantic wars between major powers erupt for actual reasons instead of endless gamey world conquest (except against uncivilized nations, which you can pretty much do with as you please, but that's historical for the time).  Even the tiniest nations are playable because you can use the crisis system to get major powers to back your claims to conquered cores.  Playing Greece and want your northern cores back from the Ottoman Empire?  You can never defeat them alone, but if you can get the United Kingdom or Russia on your side, it's entirely possible to fulfill your wildest revanchist dreams.
It has a deep (but not impenetrable), economic system that makes makes that aspect of the game very interesting and engaging, as opposed to just placing a merchent guy on the map and collecting fees.  This era saw the rise of industrialism and tycoon capitalism, and they've done that justice.
The politics system is very good as well.  Poor, middle, and elite classes all have their own wants, needs, political desires, etc. that break down to an impressively small scale.  The white yankee catholic factory workers will want one thing, while the black protestant southern miners will want something else.  If you don't handle politics smartly, you can have a revolution on your hands, which could even end with your government ideology completely changing.  It's entirely possible for the United States to become a fascist state, a Marxist-Leninist republic, or even return to monarchy.
It's simply the deepest, best, most fun game Paradox has ever released in this man's opinion.

You can play as communist Texas. 10/10.
But seriously:
Victoria II isn't the prettiest grand strategy game that's ever come around. The economic system in particular requires about seven PhDs and consultation with the Elder Gods to understand, and sometimes it feels like you don't really have any control over the politics of your country beyond slight nudges. Some would argue that's the entire point, but I digress.
Where Victoria II will grab you, and hold you, is the sheer diplomacy system. Whereas in EU4 one country will simply superblob, Vicky has a very nice system of balance. Countries rarely blob, and even when they do, they're only one catastrophic war away from being knocked down to size. And just like other Paradox games, Victoria II is incredibly easy to mod. Don't like your flag? Change it! Want to rename a political party? Change it! Feel like modifying a few provinces to balance out the economy? All that's needed is a few corrections in a text file.
PROS:
- Combat feels the most balanced of any Paradox game. Even Art of War.
- Politics system will always have you coming back for more
- Incredible attention to detail. Every country has its own republican, monarchist, fascist, and communist flag.
- Great power mechanic makes it actually feel like you're actually playing as one state among many, instead of just one human vs the same computer wearing different hats
CONS:
- Economy system is an absolute mess.
- Since Heart of Darkness, sieges take far, far too long.
FINAL VERDICT:
First off, I do NOT recommend this to anyone but gamers who have a grand strategy game or two under their belt. Anyone else is just going to take one look at the industrial and demographics screen and uninstall the game. But for those who learn its mechanics, Victoria II will pay back in dividends.

I didn't ask for this empire. I merely was designated by my predecessors to live on and carry a title. They told me that God had chosen me, but the process is the same every generation. There's war, rebellion, disease and struggle. The ruler overlooks his ash piles and tries to convice his people they can be saved. Then, through death or discontent, things fall apart.
There's no salvation for us. We were born to be a marker in history for people to use in relativity. I know there's no chance that this charade of immortality can last forever, but I can't help but want to struggle. It's as if life itself is drowning me in my own values. Every decision I make, "good" or "bad", inevitably have the same results.
There must be an answer to all of this. I scan the stacks of papers around the room. Ledgers, proposals, bribes; somewhere in here there is salvation. As another tower of writing is toppled, one letter sticks out from the bottom: a draft. As I glance over it in curiosity, I feel something I haven't felt since my second baptism. A clarity, a revelation. Somehow this beautiful, nigh-upon holy proposal was lost within this office like a treasure of biblical proportions. It was almost childlike- so much potential, so many opportunities.
For the next three days I revised and perfected the act. As the final subject came up in my council meeting, my heart jumped with excitement. This was it. This was what I've lived for all this time. I drew the sheet from my folder, and as I read it aloud, I almost couldn't believe my own words.

This is my sixth time buying this game.
The first time was for the PC. I lost the disc.
The second time was for my PS3. All PS3 ports of Bethesda games were god awful and my save file ended up getting corrupted.
The third time was probably when I was on the verge of nostalgia. It was 2014, and Oblivion had been released as a backwards compatible title for the Xbox one... They were simpler times.
The fourth time was  when I spotted the anniversary edition at my local game shop. Knowing me, I had two choices to make. I could either buy the game now, or after I got something to eat at the foodcourt. I chose the latter, thinking I could play it without any issues on my gaming computer which, at the time, consisted of a 14 Inch Macbook (no prizes for guessing the framerate).
The fifth time was for a friend who had failed to understand my obsession with this game. His playtime for Oblivion has remained at less than one hour ever since I bought it for him back in 2015.
The sixth time is now. After having the hardcopy sitting on my shelf for 2 years now without a cd-drive to insert it into my computer, I felt like it was time. It had been too long since I had set foot in the Imperial prison, and that changed now.
I believe that in every gamers life, there is always that one game that they will go back to time and time again, till the day they die. For me, Oblivion is that game.

This game is nothing like its predecessors, but it's amazing in its own right. There are so many different choices to make, so many different outcomes, a free-form hack-and-slash type of combat system, and so much lore that it can make your head spin. If you are a fan of deeply engaging stories, then this is definitely a game to try. You can play through as one of four main characters, getting the rest as partners along the way, each with their own attitudes, fighting styles, and things they agree with. You can switch between your partners at will, and they add to the story as you play through, with different pieces of insight or comments they make. The gear is completely random, but not overly terrible. There is also a nice multi-player feature where you can host your own private game or join in a public one, although you only have access to the gear the owner has acquired (as it is their game you're playing). All in all, a fantastic game with a lot of lore and plenty of replay value.

Ever played a turn-based RPG before? If you answered "yes" to any of these questions, then I have news for you: you've played this game before. It's not on your Steam library, you say? Oh, no, don't worry, it wasn't on your Steam library. This game was actually the tutorial sequence on the very first turn-based RPG you ever played. You just didn't know. You have doubts on what I'm saying? Don't worry, so do I - a Great Doubt, in fact.
"Alpha Kimori: Great Doubt - Episode 1" is the first of a turn-based RPG trilogy developed and published by Sherman3D. Let me start off by saying that this trilogy is not yet complete! Only Episodes 1 and 2 are available at the moment, and only Episode 1 is available through Steam. If you wanted to get Episode 2, it would have to be either through the
or somewhere else. But why am I talking about Episode 2 when I haven't even started talking about Episode 1? I'll touch back on that later, but for now, let's get to the meat of this thing.
The story of "Alpha Kimori: Great Doubt - Episode 1" is... umm... well, to
summarize: on a planet called Kimori there live two human tribes, the Bidarians (tech people) and the Jinrians (beast people), and they're at war! Your protagonist through this war will be Rick Brightheart, a young Bidarian who's more indecisive than a drunk CEO under stress! Rick is confused about a few things, such as why he should be fighting, who does he really care for, or if there's a bigger meaning behind all of this. I can't answer those questions, though, because that'd be spoilers. The other two main characters are Vanessa Avery and Yuki Furikai, though you technically don't find out about Yuki until a while later, but the trailer for this game reveals her name, so no point in hiding it. Personally, I found both Vanessa and Yuki to be more likeable than Rick, though that's subjective.
Now, what's the relationship between those three characters? Well, the trailer and the game's website talks a lot about a love triangle, making you believe that romance will be a huge part of the story.  And then you play it and it's... not that much about the romance. Like, it's there, but it's not the biggest nor the most interesting aspect of the game's story. Bad advertisement on Sherman3D's side. So, what is the best part about "Alpha Kimori: Great Doubt - Episode 1's" story? Well, I mentioned that Rick isn't that great of a character, but I don't
him. He starts... OK, but he does develop, and the same can be said for Vanessa and Yuki. They do have a bit of charm to them, and they'll grow on you as you keep playing. However, like the characters, the main plot - the "reality" of the war between the Bidarians and Jinrians - also takes a while to take off. The story unfortunately fails at hooking you early in the game, which results in you mostly dragging yourself through it for the first couple of hours, hoping that it'll eventually get better. Yet,
get better, and I was actually a bit surprised by that. But still, pacing could have been done a lot better.
Despite the company's name, you will not find 3D objects in this title; the game offers 16-bit styled graphics, much like classic Final Fantasy games and the sort. And in that department, it looks great! The game's colors are varied and vibrant, which is really important in keeping you at least somewhat awake during otherwise dull moments. The sprites in this game are pretty well-made, too. I was surprised to see that not only do the playable characters have custom animations, but all the enemies do as well, and they look just as good as the main cast! As far as the actual designs go, there's nothing that really blew me away, but the art-style all throughout is consistent. However, these are just the basics of graphics. As far as extra, special stuff goes, there isn't really much to talk about. There's a few particle effects here and there, none of them are noticeably impressive, and I can't seem to recall any fancy lighting effects either. Overall, I do really like the art style of the game, and I can appreciate what it does, but it doesn't do anything to put itself above the crowd.
OK, let's talk about the most important part of this review - the gameplay. I am sorry to announce that this is where the game falls the shortest. Remember when I said that you've played this game before? Well, that's because "Alpha Kimori: Great Doubt - Episode 1's" turn-based combat system is just the absolute basics of the genre: basic attack for average mobs, "Ki Attacks" for bosses, rinse and repeat. You have no status ailments to worry about, no special attributes that only affect certain enemies, etc. You have no strategy. The game doesn't even
to spice things up a bit! In turn, the game's also ridiculously easy - and short! It took me about 6 hours to beat the game, grinding constantly mind you. And the
time I actually felt challenged was with the final boss, where the difficulty just spikes out of nowhere and I actually had to think for once - which was actually great, and it just makes you wish the rest of the game was that intense! Outside of battle it's just go here, talk to so-and-so, do what they want, go talk to blah-blah-blah, bleeeeh. Levels are nice to explore the first time, but after having to revisit one area more than three times, it gets old
. Now, I will say that I can handle repetition pretty well, and leveling up in the game doesn't take too awfully long. But if you're impatient, I'm sorry, just... just skip this one.
There's a few songs in this game, and they're not bad, but you will hear them... over... and over...
You do have the option to mute the music if you get sick of it, but when muting a game's soundtrack acts as a solution to a problem, there's an issue. As far as sound effects go, I was not amused. Almost all of them are really underwhelming and don't contribute to the game's already weak immersion. I do like the main theme song for the game - "Bird" by Hatsune Miku. It's a nice little tune, I must admit. But otherwise, the sound design of this game is simply nothing special.
OK, we're getting close to the end of this review, and I have to answer the big question: do I
recommend this game? Look, this game is not for everyone. If you can't handle repetition and dull moments, stay far,
away. And personally, I wouldn't pay $10 for this game - I'd only buy it on sale (I got it from a Humble Bundle). But there's another issue: like I mentioned, this is supposed to be a trilogy. And again, Episode 2 is
available through Steam, while Episode 3 is nowhere to be found! If you do end up liking the game and want the sequel, you're going to have to go out of your way and get it from somewhere else, and probably end up paying more than you would with Steam sales (not to mention, Steam is just more convenient, honestly). Episode 2 was released back in 2012, so for the third episode to still be undone 3 years after just doesn't give me a good vibe. And I'm ashamed to admit it, but that's why I'm recommending this game. There
some potential with this franchise, and I want Sherman3D to do well so they can continue it and improve it. Even if it's not that good, this game does have a certain charm to it; you can tell it's a very humble product from a very humble company, and it does feel like they put their heart into developing it. I'm not too awfully fond of just Episode 1 alone, but I do want to see the Alpha Kimori franchise grow. But that's just hopeful thinking on my part. I recommend this game

This is a great game for beginners and those who want to have fun.
Alas an RPG is only as good as its story and characters, and this is where the game makes its greatest mistake. The story is not bad, but it is mediocre. You also only get one weapon upgrade which you get from the characters automatically just buy shields and maybe some armor. By the way save all your items for the final battle and it will be easy.  I could go on with the list of problems, but I feel as if this is one of the better RPG Maker games.
