"The Curious Expedition" is a game I've been following for a while, but felt quite hesitant about reviewing until now. At the time of writing this, the game is at Alpha 13 and about 40% done if I had to gauge it myself: the fine details and overall "feel" of the game are already making it very much alive, but its balance is broken to the point where I would not recommend playing it if you're not well-versed in roguelikes and looking for something to seriously break your head into.
But that's pretty much the only bad thing I have to say about it.
The Curious Expedition is a boatload of fun, employing a theme that is practically an epitome of the genre, and packing a lot of excitement for players who are willing to take the right risks and perform a very minimal amount of micro-management. Almost every run is story-worthy in its own right, and you don't have to stray too far from this review section to get a sense of how quickly and hilariously♥♥♥♥♥♥can hit the fan if you're not careful (or just unlucky).
I would recommend this game, at its current stage of development, to fans of the genre who are looking for a very refreshing up-and-comer.

TCE is a procedural rogue-like exploration game that provides you with plenty of difficult but meaningful decisions to make as you lead a party on a series of dangerous and often ill-fated expeditions into uncharted territory. You'll meet natives, ransack shrines, explore caves, fight wild beasts, loot cool items, level up your party members, and occasionally eat those party members to survive.
If you're unable to see past the 16-bit style graphics to enjoy the epic adventurous narrative the games brilliant design allows you to create for yourself, TCE is probably not the game for you. But if you're a gamer's gamer, more concerned with making meaningful choices that could very well result in very tragic consequences, you'll find TCE refreshingly challenging.
Do you waste an inventory slot/funds on dynamite you may never use but will wish you had if you get trapped inside mountains?
Do you drink whiskey when getting low on sanity, even though your Scottish soldier is already and alcoholic and could only get worse?
Do you ransack the ancient altar to find loot, when you know it will upset your native animal handler who is giving your mounts a huge carrying bonus?
Do you explore that cave even though the cultist in your party has developed claustraphobia?
Do you rest overnight at that native village when your British soldier is an unapologeteic racist?
The answers to all of these questions are almost always yes. But you make these choices accepting the consequences, because the alternative is often far worse. And this is the brilliance of TCE and why I highly reccomend it.

Let's Play: Tavernier
Tavernier is a great little game that combines tavern management with what feels like a classic childhood choose your own adventure book. You inherit a tavern and it is your job to turn a profit while deciding what groups of townspeople to support. The gamepley itself is very simple and easy to pickup. Each turn, depending on the amount of coin you have, you can unlock more items to sell, purchase decorations to help increase your tavern rating and cashflow, or buy more furniture to allow more patrons access to your tavern (tavern management). Once you have finished this, you click a button to advance time one week and are presented with a random event for which you must choose a response (choose your own adventure). The choice you make generally does not have major consequences to the game and rather affects patronage of a group or your coin reserves. It then shows you your cashflow and you do it again for the next game week. This is basically the game.
-PROS:
- Artstyle is unique and enjoyable
- Easy to pickup and learn quickly
- Good story and content for price
- High replayability value
- Steam Achievements
-CONS:
- Short storyline
- Could use more objects and food to buy
- Random event choices dont really matter overall
TLDR: Great little game for the price. Absolutely recommend!!!!

Each of the routes had their own particular charms, which surprised me, and my own expectations of which routes I'd prefer turned out to be totally wrong due to the strength of the story and the characterizations.
Localization for the game is very good.  For me, poor localization, typos, and awkward phrasing completely breaks immersion for me in visual novels.  In Amnesia, I can't even remember any awkward phrases, and I found only two typos during my entire playthrough.
The game does suffer from situations where the protagonist's actions (or lack thereof) defy common sense, though the use of Orion, her onboarded spirit, actually does help.  Orion tends to embody a lot of the inner dialogue (and outrage) of the gamer, embodying sentiments such as "how dare he say that!" that the protagonist unfortunately doesn't really ever act upon.  Amnesia also suffers from the common visual novel ailment where as the player it can be virtually impossible to know how to avoid bad ends.  There were thankfully less of these than in some other games I've played, but I did find it often frustrating how a single choice led to a bad end that the game gave me no reasonable clues to predict.  Similarly, I found the good ends frustrating to get because they didn't really follow obvious choice paths.
Overall though, Amnesia is definitely worth the asking price.  It has many hours of gameplay and for any otome fans out there, it's one of the highest quality otome games I've played here in the West.  When playing, I couldn't put it down and basically marathoned the game for a week, and was left wanting more.  (Please bring the sequels to the West, Idea Factory!!).

This Game. Just, this game.
If you're planning on getting this game at the moment, don't let anything put you off. When I was a lot younger, owning this game on the PS3 [Yes, I am still one of those little turds who still attend school], I didn't like it. But now? It's one of the best games I've played in a while.  So if you're new to this series, here's a review for you to settle you in. Well, as best as I can.
So the plot is simple: Abe, the Mudokon who was formerly a floor-waxer for Rupture Farms before blowing it up, finds out of a despicable plan by the Glukkons through a group of dead spirits named The Three Weirdos. The burial ground of Necrum had been stolen from; bones were being mined by blinded Mudokons, as they were a required ingredient or the well-known beverage Soulstorm Brew. Upon finding this out, Abe sets out to Destroy the brewery and stop this new industrialist scheme. An okay plot, if I say so myself, despite being along similar lines as Oddysee.
The gameplay is quite something. So let's get this out the way. Abe's normal controls, walking, running, rolling, jumping and all sorts are really smooth in a sense. They're responsive and flow well with the pace of the game, whether it be slow platforming or heart-pounding chases, and trust me, there are going to be lots of those. You're probably going to spend a lot of the time either walking, rolling or sneaking, as running is mainly essential for chases with Sligs, Scrabs and Paramites, which do crop up at just the right times. Jumping is precise and easy to do, y'just press the space button and you'll leap about two to three spaces forwards, which you learn and can pretty much master right off the bat. In fact, most movement CAN be learnt that quickly. And sneaking is just walking, 'cept Sligs can't hear you. Dead simple, and with a noise I can't get out of my head for some reason.
Gamespeak. This nifty mechanic allows Abe to talk to his enslaved race and lead them to bird portals. A lot are simple: Hello, follow me, all of ya', wait, all that stuff. However, replacing the whistling from the last game, there are now options to slap, say sorry, tell people to stop. This was because in this game, the Mudokons have several emotions to work around, going from sad and angry, the blind Mudokons who will follow the sound of your voice but not you, or sick Mudokons who you have to heal with ring powers. There isn't much else to say here. Nifty.
Posession is something that got a direct upgrade adding even MORE experimentation. Unlike last game where you could only posess Sligs, the gun-toting cyborg henchmen of the Magog Cartel, you can posess EVERYTHING here. Well, except for slogs. Scrabs? Check. Paramites? Check. The Glukkons who you can use to order around Sligs to do your bidding? Checkedy Checkedy Check. These all have their own curveballs, own Gamespeak, and own uses. Even though there aren't too many times you can posess Glukkons, and Phleg... Oh god, that part in Bonewerkz.
This is where the game gets sublime. And by sublime, I mean some of the best atmosphere, music and art direction you're going to see. The score matches your enviroment perfectly. A few I can list off the top of my head are Necrum, the Mines, the Mudanchee & Mudumo Vaults, and then FeeCo Depot. Be it tribal instruments clashing and meshing to get the feel of a sacred area, or the mechanical and almost oppresive sounds of industrial areas like Necrum Mines or Soulstorm Brewery. All these tracks accompany the backgrounds perfectly. The amount of detail put into these images, the sheer
clearly poored into this was worth the time, creating truly stunning pieces of art, such as all the areas involving the vaults or Necrum, which capture the sacred yet barren forest which has long been forgotten. This doesn't have to be the background either. Character animations, like the floor-wiping Mudokon slaves or even the mere act of climbing ledges or entering doors, are animated as smoothly and realistic as they possibly could be.
For all the good things I've had to say about this game, there is at least one problem with the game, albeit not being a major flaw with the game. This game can be hard. Not just your standard quite challenging levels cropping up a few times, no. Each and every section of this game will have at least one finger-numblingly difficult puzzle or level or just segment. It can either be you can't figure a situation out or you're stuck in one of the game's many chases where you have to run from hostile wildlife and the slimy tentacle cyborgs with machineguns. Only a minor problem, but this will cause a lot of pain.
Well, what do I think of the game? It is timeless. A truly gorgeous blast from the past which will continue to amaze for quite some time, even if the newer games like Oddworld: Soulstorm flop! [Which I best will be nowhere near happening] If you're thinking about getting this game, go ahead. Only 1.99 pound, or at least for us English, and well worth the small amount of money you take out of your pockets to pay. a 10/10 from yours not so truly, some random person on the internet you probably hate.

I absolutely love this game. I love it so much, I spent a month only playing this game and saved all the Mudokans. TL,DR

Crusader Kings II is probably one of the greatest strategy games I ever played. While the many features this game offers may seem overwhelming at first one quickly gets the basics that are enough to play. And after that, the player slowly learns more and more.  But this is in my opinion one of the things that make this game so charming.
What's also great is how diverse different campaigns can be because of different random events and the fact that there is no predertemined goal. Whether you plan to convert the whole world to your religion, control the biggest empire in history or just live a happy life with a big loving dynasty, the possibilities are endless.
Still there are two things I want to criticize: First of all, as mentioned, getting into the game can be hard at first and one might lose interest quickly. However, once you get basics you have access to one of the greatest strategy games with RPG elements that there is.
Second is Paradox's DLC policy. This isn't just a problem with CKII but also with other Paradox games. If you want to own all DLC packs that there are you have to pay multiple hundred bucks, even on sale.
There is not a single person who can forget that kings and queens can get invaded by the americas, thats this game.
Want to play as a small Irish count and conquer all of Western Europe, well you probably won't succeed, but if you want to try this is the game for you.

- Mods:
This game has a passionate fanbase, think of something, there is probably a mod for that, though game of throne mod is def one of the best mods out there
- Developers:
Sure you want to scream at them sometimes for the price of that DLC, or a frustrating mechanic, but in the end, the day, they do a good job, it's no miracle that this game has been around for so long, they keep  adding features that truly enhance the game
Get it on sale, and you'll love it

In Victoria 2, you play as a nation for 100 years, starting in 1836.
The game primarily revolves around the "pops" (a simulation of your population), who can have various jobs, purchase goods, and migrate around the world. As you play the game, you'll be industrializing your country by researching techs, building factories, and conquering other (usually less advanced) areas of the world in order to procure goods for your factories. You also have to deal with the various political ideologies which will cause your subjects to demand various government reforms, or even to openly revolt in order to attempt to enforce whatever ideology they follow (democratic reforms, communism, etc.).
Pros:
-fun to see an alternate history play out
-pop system is well done and adds a human character to the game
-interesting events, but not so many big random ones as in other games, so overall there is less luck at play
-mod support. there are some excellent mods available which flesh out the game even more.
Cons:
-some parts of the economy simulator are kind of strange. it works ok, but feels a little unrealistic at times.
-combat involves dice rolls, which imo is not the greatest thing. That being said they don't have an overwhelming effect so it isn't too luck based
-doesn't have very good UI, which can be confusing.
-AI can be somewhat stupid in certain situations.
Overall I would recomend this game to anyone who likes longer and slower strategy games. Some important things to note for anyone interested in playing this are:
1. Like all paradox games, there is no real set objective, and you are expected to set your own goals. There is a ranking system which makes it more possible to feel like you "won" by getting to the #1 spot, but it's not like say Civilization with victory conditions. If you prefer a more focused objective, this may not be the game for you.
2. Be sure to purchase all the expansions. Unlike some later releases like Crusader Kings, where each new DLC is accompanied by a free patch, many of the expansions for this contain fixes to balance and such. You can still have fun without them of course, but the game may be a little strange.
3. The interface is a bit complicated and can feel a bit overwhelming initially. Combined with the fact that there is no "winning", you may begin to feel like you are just sitting there doing nothing when you first play. My advice is to quickly go through the menus to get an idea of your options, and after that, don't worry about it too much and just start playing. You will likely make some stupid mistakes but overall you should be fine as long as you are playing a decently powerful country. Also, try to set smaller objectives as you go along rather than setting some huge goal at the start - this will keep things less stressful for your first game.

This is a hard game to love, but I do. I've sunk far too much time into it to say I don't love it. It can be extremely fun but also very infuriating.
It's meant to be a casual side-scrolling Moba / Dota-clone and it does that very well, but when I say casual, I mean super casual. Not caring about winning and game-breaking issues casual.
I can handle losing just fine and I couldn't care less about ranking. Being out-played and out-maneuvered comes with any online game. You play until you get better. What I can't handle is losing because you can go 1v3 or the drop-in / drop-out system forcing you to be always down a player because someone forgot they left the oven on and the next person just got a call, so your 3rd is constantly on their way to fight. Or the terrible matchmaking making you join a game where everyone has 300+ ping (yes you can set the game to find only local players but the player base is so small I've had that take 15+ minutes. And then the game is force-started because someone is too impatient).
There's issues involving lag even in local region games that have been around since game launch and continue to persist and will forever persist, because the game uses a p2p hosting model instead of a dedicated server. That cost cutting measure is simply awful and I've been dropped out of MANY games where the host decides to leave and we can't all get connected to the new host, sometimes resulting in the entire match being scrapped.
I've played the game since almost launch, contributed far too much money to the expansion kickstarter and bought some DLC I didn't care about just to support the devs.  But I've also uninstalled 6-8 times and quit for months at a time because all the issues got to be too much.
I usually come back after a big patch rollout hoping some more issues are solved, but more often than not it's simply some unless flair added to the GUI and some balance changes which I can rarely understand the reasoning behind.
I've ragged on it a lot and I'm not giving it a thumbs up (in its current state), but I do recommend picking it up, maybe on sale and giving it a shot. Maybe it will have most of my issues with it fixed and if not, at least you can get some good hours out of it.

I highly recommend playing this fantastic otome/visual novel game! It's a must have for people who like these sort of games!!
After watching the anime back in 2013 and finding out that this game would come out in 2015, I was extremely happy... so after managing to 100% the game, I have to offically say that this is one of my favorite game series of all time! (Now hurry up and release the sequels for us impatient fans!! [Later, Crowd and World]).
With this being my 2nd otome game that I'd play and with this game already having very high praise from Japan, I was very excited to jump into this new and exciting world where I will finally get the whole story of this universe. Oh how I was impressed with the way this game gave off a very care-free choice option off the bat.
Want to be serious and make a good and believe able example of yourself as the MC of this otome game, or do you want to be as unserious and awkward as possible and make your boyfriend suspicious of you? The choice is all there, especially when you get to chose between 4 (actually 5) worlds off the bat!
I was actually a little anxious that the MC would be one of those annoying, way too obvious or innocent type of girl... sure she is in the beginning, but once she remembers more memories and gets to understand how her boyfriend acts, she manages to remember her personality and is actually very likeable (you even get to see this by the options you have to chose to interact with different people).
Because of the free reign, it made the story progress very smoothly. There were no unnesecary moments/fillers (if there were they were either fluff moments where the boyfriend is acting all cute or comedy moments to shake off a little drama when it became too much) when playing through the different worlds, which again made each route and ending very enjoyable. And since it's a straight up visual novel, it makes the game very relaxing to play, as if you were going to watch an anime.
Finished all the routes? Why not go for ALL the possible endings? ...Still not enough? Then go ahead and go to your gallery and get some secret messages when you Ctrl+click on rose images where your chosen dream boyfriend whispers sweet-nothingness into your ear as they keep complaining about you clicking on them. Wow, still not satisfied when you have clickable boys and extra fluff memories? Well then air hockey and rock-paper-scissor might just be your thing!
The ammount of work, time and passion which went through with making this game is unbeliveable to grasp compared to how other games today are released. And this game was released in 2011 in Japan! I still can't thank Idea Factory enough, I couldn't help myself than to buy their limited edition box of this game to support them even more.
Anyway, to sum it all up:
PROS:
* Characters
* Beautiful Artstyle (especially the unique eyes)
* Pro voice acting
* Very interesting and good story for each of the characters
* Music
* Mini Games + extra CG/Gallery hidden story (extras unlock once you get every ending!!)
* Achivements
CONS:
* Minor visual/gameplay bugs when quick speeding (but this almost never happened or it recently got patched)
* Too few save slots
* Can't replay any kind of endings on the good/normal and bad ending list
Overall score: 9/10

I love this game. Having been a long time lover of the Sid Meier's Civilization series this game is a wonderful mix of the familiar civilization building and the unexpected.  I think Endless Legend is everything that I was hoping to get from Beyond Earth and more. I highly reccomend it.

Endless Legend is one of the better games I've played in a while.  It was easier to understand than Endless Space though I do like that one also due to the very good tutorial in Endless Legend.  I went through the complete tutorial as it explains how to do everything in the game.  The game is very much Civilization like in that you build the buildings and military you want in your city.  You can also grow your city larger by building Boroughs.  Each section or area of the map can contain only 1 city so there is no need to figure out the spacing between your cities.  There are a variety of races to choose from.  Each Race only has 3 different Military units that you can build but if you Assimilate a Minor Faction you can also build their military units also.  You can also upgrade the 3 Different Military unit choices you have with better weapons and armor and items which all the units of that type that you build in the future will have.  Your Armies or cities can also be led by heroes who level up and gain new abilities when they do through the assigning of skill points.  You can taylor your Hero to be better at giving a city food, dust or production for instance or you can make your hero a Military killing machine by making the armies he leads have greater life or attack , etc.  Heros and other units can also engage in quests through exploring ruins which adds a small role playing element to this beautiful 4X strategy game.  Everything is turn based and you can fight combat in turn based mode to have more control or just put it on Auto combat.  At first I fought everything in turn based combat to micromanage my troops but I found it sped up the game by going to automatic combat and the computer did a pretty good job of accessing losses.  You also have faction quests you can complete and if you finish them you can build a wonder and win the wonder victory.  I highly recommend this game for any gamer but especially those who like Sid Meier's Civilization games.  This game is far better than Beyond Earth and Endless Space is far better than Beyond Earth.  This games compare more favorably to the actual Civilization titles like Civ 5, civ 1, 2,3,4.

Growing up, I enjoyed playing an old DOS game called "The Lost Tribe." I enjoyed this game a lot and wished it would be remade. "The Curious Expedition" is the closest thing I would get to that and it's awesome! The Curious Expedition is a strategy and resource management game with an Indiana Jones theme. You explore exotic regions around the world in search of treasures, fame, and fortune. Much like The Lost Tribe, you move from tile to tile across the map in order to find the end location. In Tribe, it was a volcano. In Expedition, it's a golden pyramid. Comparing both games, Expedition is somewhat easier than Tribe. But both games offer plenty of challenge and a lot of fun. I really recommend picking up The Curious Expedition and giving it a try!

Do you feel lucky?
No, really, do you? Because the answer to that question is, incidentally, also the answer to whether you would enjoy this game.
You can have an expedition loaded down with golden idols, anthropological studies, paintings, mummies, and elite expeditioners, only to run out of sanity and chocolate one leg before the golden pyramid, and immediately lose it all to cannibalism. Or you can run out of chocolate several days before the pyramid and nothing happens. All a matter of luck.
And the later expeditions only rely on luck more, when, in order to enter the golden pyramid and thus end the expedition, you have to find moonstones, and good luck with that, because if you don't happen to find the approximately three places in your region where there might be moonstones, then you are going to die.
If you are not too upset at having your successes crumble away before you due to events completely beyond your control, then it's not too bad a game. I enjoy it, somewhat, but I would not recommend it to most people.

I love the ambiance of the tavern, the music is nice, and the artwork is coherent.
The story is interesting when you play for the first time, but it might lack some replayability since there aren't any major gameplay changes if you follow a different starting faction - the additional factions bring some refreshment though. Also, the post-end gameplay isn't very rich - I guess it's intended, but I have the feeling you only get access to a small number of events which repeat themselves.
The gameplay itself is quite immersive, and the tutorial allows you to get the knack of it quickly enough, even though the first run might be difficult because of events you don't expect and storyline prerequisites you don't understand / aren't prepared to reach. The concept of the tavern management, with a storyline to follow is quite innovative, and I found it to be a great experience.

Great little choose-your-own-adventure game, very worth the small price.  The art style looks nice, and the writing got more than a few chuckles out of me.  There are even nice atmospheric touches like changing the look of the tavern as the game progresses and giving you new music about halfway through (to give you a break from the track you've probably been playing for the past half hour).
It took me two playthroughs and a little over an hour and a half to figure out how to get to the end of the story, but there are several factions you can focus on, so I'll probably play through it a few more times just to see more of the dialogues.  If you find you're stuck, use the "management" mode instead of story mode.  It'll show the rewards of all possible actions, so you can make better decisions about how to build the stats you need.

Tavernier combines RPG and management elements to create an engaging, short & sweet story in which you can choose how you wish to run your tavern. Be a cool, small-folk friendly tavern owner, get palsy with local soldiers, or befriend spirits, the choice is yours!
Throughout the course of my first gameplay I've managed to:
- Acquire a chic lead statue decoration
- Learn magic
- Play choir live music
- Harbour a forbidden Twilight-ish romance
- Rig a local election
- Upset a hen customer
- Allow a mage patron to pull a Jesus in my bar
Failed to be a good tavernier anyway, but I'll definitely do another round.

With a decent variety of choices that affects the story, Tavernier is an excellent story-rich RPG that's worth a lot more than $2. Highly recommended.

Overall I really enjoyed this game, but like a lot of otome games it has some problematic aspects along with the good ones.
First, the art is really beautiful even if the characters' outfits are completely, hilariously absurd. All of the sprites and CGs are really pretty, and the backgrounds are sort of a muted colors with white.
Unlike some otome games where you spend the first part of the game getting to know the characters and then figuring out which ones you want to romance, this game makes you choose immediately and then you are locked into that guy's route and can only succeed or fail (spectacularly) at it.
The good part about this is that the stories for each guy are very different, and as your character starts with amnesia (like the title) the mysterious and unknown parts of your life are different between routes. The relationships you have to the love interests and other characters change, which is really interesting and gives the game a lot of replayability since each route is basically its own thing.
The stories are all very engaging, but there are some definite yandere aspects to some of the relationships, so if that isn't your cup of tea you may want to look into which guys have that before playing so that you can avoid those routes. Or choose them, I guess, if you want to be locked in a cage by a possessive crazy person. :)
The bad ends definitely kill you, and since the MC has amnesia, she does tend to fall into the otome heroine trope of being fairly passive. There's a story reason for it, obviously, but if you're looking for a spunky MC with her own personality you won't find that here. MC has a few moments, but she's clearly intended to be pretty bland so that you can read whatever you want into her.
I recommend this game, it's a beautiful game with an engaging story, but it's definitely a Japanese otome game in a lot of ways which can be a good or  bad thing depending on how you look at it.

I love the concept behind this game. It's kind of like playing Civilisation V but it has so many unique features that it does kind of feel like a different game altogether. At first, going in with this perspective - I have to admit, I didn't like it. It felt a bit like a poor rip off of the game. Delving into it and giving it a chance anyway, I found that actually I like it quite alot. There are certain aspects from the whole territory dividing feature which gives it a unique twist, a restriction that can be described as welcome (otherwise acquiring resources would be not nearly as challenging) to things like being able to customise your own race. This feature is probably one that is not liked by others, and I can't imagine how it would fare if you played for serious competitivity but between friends - feels like a nice little charm seeing the different strategies that your friends will implement to succeed, whether it be from the quite commonly seen choice of tweaking a class that has already been described by the game itself as Broken or from doing something slightly creative and creating a peace loving clan that unites itself in peace with all bar one to single that clan out and abolish them from the game.
(Note to Creators should you ever read this: Please don't ever balance this. I don't mind that it is clear that some races have a typical advantage because that creates creative solutions as to how to overcome them - and I always have found games where balancing happens too frequently to become very bland and lack excitement. That moment when you discover something really cool about a race that gives you a clear advantage over others can really contribute to that feeling of something special when playing any game).
The music is brilliant, and has an atmospheric aura that only contributes to the game - I am a fan of the originally created audio in most games, my friends however - not so much. But even they have stated that this game doesn't have one of those repetitive audio tracks that begin to get on your nerves after a while but actually can be listened to and enjoyed throughout the playthrough of the game.
The graphics are a lovely touch as well, they update every time you re-tab into the game which is great and they look and feel great. They really contribute again to the atmosphere that you're playing in a war as opposed to some kind of arcade themed strategy game. They clearly have had quite some time put into them too and it's a nice touch - even better that you can play the game with these graphics even on a lower spec computer like my own without experiencing too many issues.
One problem I do have with the game though (well actually two, a minor and a major). The syncing issue in multiplayer (being the minor problem) can be a little annoying sometime. I have recently learned that this is likely due to the spec of my computer and so isn't too great an issue but I've noticed for some reason it flags off as unsynced but we can still play for ages anyway. I don't mind ignoring and haven't rated the score I gave accordingly - but thought I'd mention it anyway.
The problem that I marked the score down for was the way the game is mapped? I don't know if that's the correct terminology but basically when you try to assign the moves of some of your units, sometimes you'll have to remouse over the tile you want a few times (only happens sometimes, so not unbearable). I'm not sure if this is related to terrain mapping but it's a little annoying and has caused me to make a few poor choices by accident. The problem with this is it does contribute to giving the game a little bit of a laggy feel sometimes (also noticeable in the main menu selection as well by the way) which is a shame because it's a tiny feature which lets the game down a tiny bit - especially on first impressions, which if I was a different type of gamer, could have caused me to simply reject the game on that impression alone.
Overall, the game is amazing though. I don't want to end on a bad note and I only rated it two lower in the hope for an aspiration for improvement from the developers. The game is great and I'm really enjoying it so far. I would like to see more classes, units and technologies, as well as more factions but I guess that's what DLC is for. I eagerly await the expansions.

I could almost recommend this game based only on its slick interface. It is probably the best interface in any turn-based strategy game ever.
A strong point this game has over other turn-based strategy games is a technology system which allows you to adapt to your surroundings and playstyle. I.e if you don't intend to go to war, you don't need to pick an sort of military tech to advance your civilization. If you have a lot of rivers, you could pick a tech that improves their output. It is a great system for players who like devloping unique minmaxing strategies, and gives the game a lot of replayability. The same faction with two different sets of technological choices play very differently.

Have you ever been so completely immersed in a game, loving every minute of it and every minute detail, only to be smacked in the face by a huge glaring issue that makes you not want to play the game again? The AI in this game is the guilty case in this scenario for me. Despite previously making a 4X strategy game (Endless Space) and an expansion for it (along with a year or more of updates), Amplitude for some reason forgot to teach the AI basic strategies. For example: in my most recent game, I found another faction roughly three regions away from me who was neutral towards me. They then proceded to send a settler into my territory, yell at me when I attacked it, settled a city (after retreating with the settler), and then begged for mercy when I steamrolled their defenseless city. After agreeing to a cease fire, they then chastised me for controlling territory next to them (the city I just captured). The most baffling part of this is that the AI seems to be as bad if not worse than vanilla Endless Space's AI. I would've expected going into this that Endless Legend should have playable AI after the dev's previous experience.
On top of the terrible (unplayable?) AI, you have tons of network issues. Even with just one other person, the game can still desync or crash if someone's connection has even a lag spike. Although its a nice touch to have drop-in-drop-out gameplay in a 4X, joining a friend's 3 player game to replace an AI ended up desyncing the rest of them and effectively ended the game since they hadn't saved yet. There is an option to resync the connections but it doesn't seem to ever work properly for me or any of my friends.
Often times I feel like I am fighting with the game itself to make my cities do more than one thing at a time; each of the 4 "X's" requires absolute focus in Endless Legend. Although I love the struggle against the planet itself, I wish I could disable certain handicaps. Ramping research cost for all tech (including previous eras), paying influence to engage in diplomacy, and winter's random increasingly powerful debuffs and durations are just a few of the wrenches the game throws into your nation's machine. An eventual endless winter comes if you play for a very long match, causing your production and troops to slow to a crawl. I understand from a lore standpoint you have to make the game difficult to play against, but even SMAC's Alpha Centauri was more hospitable than Auriga.
Outside of the AI and network issues, Endless Legend is fantastic. I love the unique popup map layout (reminiscent of Game of Thrones's intro), deep levels of zoom, a creative twist on combat that combines the best of old and new 4X combat systems, and harshness of the game environment. I really want to like this game but as of now I can only recommend it for 4X enthusiasts with a LAN. Hopefully the devs continue working on improving the AI and we won't need to wait until an expansion to "buy" working AI.

Let's start with the bad: Sometimes it feels like Digital Extremes made a fun game by accident. When it works, it's fantastic--but be ready to uninstall and reinstall it every few weeks, because it will break for seemingly no reason. The devs don't play their own game, and it shows. It'd be nice if they hired some additional programmers to go back and fix some of the more egregious bugs and failures, since the main team's determined to continue cranking out new stuff as fast as possible--but I won't hold my breath, and neither should you.
All flaws aside, it's worth playing, and p.much the best free-to-play game out there. The learning curve is mostly reasonable--although they did hide the absolutely crucial parkour tutorial deep in the Codex--and the weapons are differentiated from one another fairly well, as opposed to just having 50 guns with the exact same stats like some other games do. The eponymous Warframes each have their own specialties, strengths, and weaknesses, and while there are several different frames that can fill each basic niche, they all put their own spin on it. The community is mostly relaxed and competent--but if you don't feel like dealing with randos from the matchmaking system, almost everything in the game can be soloed with the right setup.
If you need a timesink, you can do a hell of a lot worse.

This is probably the worst game I have ever played in my life.
The game is essentially a wheres waldo style of game, you cannot tell that from watching the trailer but it is.  Here is how the game works.
Your dropped into a fairly large level and have to find a red robot to kill.  When you kill the red robot he drops an item.  Bring this item to the generator located somewhere in the level.  When you do, all the enemies respawn including the red robot.  The catch is the red robots location is completely random, so you have to search through the level until you find him again.  You have to repeat this process...TEN times, yes you read that right, 10 times.  After the 10th time you get a key to open a door.  When you open this door you are given another key to open a door on the opposite side of the level, open that door and you are given an item which you bring to the starting point and that nukes the board allowing you to progress.
The next level is exactly the same only the red robot is replaced with an orange rock monster.
I don't know how anyone could have thought this game would be fun, I don't know how anyone thought that wandering around a huge level finding a randomnly placed enemy 10 times in a row would be enjoyable by anyone.  I kept playing because I was in a state of shock that a person actually thought this would be a good idea for a game, sat down for god knows how long to make the game, and then have the nerve to charge people real money for it.  I was willing to ignore the stolen assets, the terrible control scheme, and the foggy graphics to give this game a legit shot, but the design here is flawed beyond belief and I cannot imagine anyone enjoying this.

Is this game fun, Well yes. BUT there are somethings that need to change in order for this game to truely be a good game.
Pros.
The game perfectly captures the moba spirit, but in a fast paced action platformer. Don't like RTS style constant clicking? Think there's not enough action in Dota or league of legends? This game has it.
Voice acting and soundtrack are great.
artstyle is nice and fresh
The game IS fun.
Negatives.
This game can not be competitive yet. There are numerous reasons why, but let's start off with the worst offenders.
1. There is no strategy to picking a character. None. There isn't a draft, so you can't see what the other team is going to pick. It's like Blind pick in league of legends. There's a reason for that mode not being ranked. If the other team happens to pick a character that counters yours, you're screwed the entire game.
I propose something like league of legends. Each team can ban 1 character, and they take turns picking their characters while the one they picked is shown to both teams. Until this is implemented, If you are looking for a serious competition, go look elsewhere.
2. The Paywall.
What Paywall? The expansion. I'm fine with them having an expansion. That isn't the issue. Here's the issue. Almost all of the expansion characters have a attack that passes through the turrets. Normally, you can use the turret as a shield to take some damage while you fight off the enemy team. A lot of the characters in the expansion have attacks that can go through said turret. nibbs, Penny, Ted McPain (in levels that have the turrets on top of the jungle area), sentry x58 has an attack that draws you in from behind the turret. You see where I'm going with this? Ok. So there are characters that can get you behind the turret. There must be one that can in the normal game too, right? Yeah, there is. One. Coco. So if you have the expansion, you can poke the heck out of anyone behind the turret, but if you just have the base game? Just pray there's a coco on your team or you're screwed because you can't touch them.
3. Joining late games.
The game has bots take over after someone leaves. That's awesome and well needed in other mobas. You know what isn't awesome? Other players can then join the game and replace these bots. I've had numerous times where I'd join a game, only to find out all the turrets were gone for us and the whole team had rage quit so I'm the only one there. A garenteed lose. Gee, thanks. Unfortunately this happens WAY to often. You get screwed just for wanting to play the game! If people still want that feature, fine. Put a switch in there that you can click and say "I only want to join NEW games. NOT games in progress." This sucks.
4. Disconnections. The game gives you a penalty for quiting the game. This is good. Unfortunately, You can't rejoin games that you have disconnected from. Internet goes down for a second? Congrats, you are now punished when you start another game.  Game crashes? Punished. Fair, right? You should be able to rejoin games that you we disconnected from. Simple as that.
Summary:
This game is fun. I always have a good match or two when playing. But, because of these problems, I can't recommend this game. These issues need to be fixed before this game is good enough to recommend to anyone.

Awesomenauts is a great 2D MOBA platformer. The game is run with P2P multiplayer, which means that occasionally there are lag issues, depending on the host of the game; however, if the lag issues are bad, the game often switches to a better host. While competitive, I still find it to be much more relaxed than other MOBAs like LoL or DOTA 2. There are many characters available and there's always a playstyle and character for everyone. The voice actors for the game are often popular Youtubers and the voices and dialogue make the game hilarious at times.
Although you do have to unlock characters by playing games and leveling up, the starting characters provide valuable insight into how the rest of the characters work. Each character has a unique jump and movement speed and the first two characters allow new players to learn about how to use the different jumps and speeds they may encounter later.
Many players complain about a few "overpowered" characters. The truth, in my opinion, is that every character is overpowered if used well, which results for an interesting balance in the game. However, Ronimo often updates and rebalances the characters as needed, and adds new characters every now and then.
The community is usually quite pleasant with a few exceptions once in awhile; however, there is no voice chat (looking at the mute buttons that are now available on the scoreboard, that may be soon to come) and players rarely type in chat. Teamplay with friends is highly recommended, but not necessary. Personally, I am a solo queuer, meaning that I just join in to a game by myself, and it works out pretty well.
Awesomenauts is an amazing and addictive game and I've been playing it every day since I bought it months ago. If you've never played a MOBA before, this is a great game to start with (I was an FPS gamer before this game). I highly recommend this game for anyone just looking to have fun, but there are competitive leagues if you're interested in that as well. Collapse

Another really cool feature is that when you clear a route, you can click certain spots on certain images in the gallery for that character to hear new voiced tidbits (and yes, they are subtitled). If you are a fan of otome or just want to play a really great visual novel with a hint of suspense and mystery, buy this game!

An extremely well-made otome game with intriguing storylines and gorgeous artwork. In this, you play as a young woman who has lost her memories. With the help of a young spirit, you must navigate the world around you in order to figure out who your enemies are and who you can trust.
This is a wonderful game and I sincerely hope that we start to get more translations of popular Japanese otome games on here. Every route in Amnesia is completely different, so at no point was I bored reading through the stories. Highly recommended.
The Romance Options:
-Diamond: Toma - aka Mr. Yandere, was extremely disturbing. Not my cup of tea, but the other routes made up for his storyline.
-Heart: Shin - a childhood friend and a storyline that plays out like a detective story. This one was my favorite out of all the stories. I loved Shin, which was unexpected. Going into the game I had expected to like Ikki the best.
-Spade: Ikki - a playboy who has a "condition" where anyone who looks into his eyes falls in love with him. An interesting story that I enjoyed, even if I wanted to shake Ikki most of the time.
-Clubs: Kent - aka the Vulcan option. If you think Spock is hot, then Kent'll be right up your ally. This is probably the one route that was straight romance without a major plot thread involving murder mysteries, supernatural abilities, or crazy yandere boyfriends.
-Joker: I don't want to give much away for this route. All I'll say is that I enjoyed this one a lot. It ties together all of the storylines you've read by the time you get to this point.

Let me preface this by saying that I'm positive about it because I don't feel I ought to judge an indie developer releasing their game for free according to the same standard that I would judge a larger studio. My feedback is almost for the developer more than it is for any actual players, so there are spoilers, and if you're trying to figure out whether or not to spend your time playing, maybe read a different review.
There's some really unique and engaging content in this title. A few of the puzzles, a few of the moments really stuck with me. In particular, the level 'Park' was my favorite, even though it ran laggy for me. The silent conversation between you and the clock was composed of two unique elements--the silent flashes of text, which felt like someone trying to stealthily communicate with me without tipping off some higher power, and the response-less typing, in a similar vein. If the scene had felt plugged into some large story, it would have been ever better.
The story is really where it just barely falls short, or seems to. I wasn't able to finish the game, but what I saw felt a little like something that was trying to be Stanley Parable, but was throwing together scenes that seemed to have an 'unusual/dream' vibe, rather than having a firm idea of where it was going and what it was trying to convey.
Unfortunately, during the level 'Immensity' I became too frustrated to continue. The engine didn't seem well suited to platforming. Even when I turned the graphics quality down, I died a good dozen times trying to jump from platform to platform. Eventually I couldn't see any hope of ever finding and breaking all those little jars. The section involving running around in the dark was also more annoying than enjoyable.

My donkey and I journeyed on. I took comfort in his presence. I greatly enjoyed his sense of humour and the way he laughed and cursed me in his horrible demonic voice. When I met a friendly native tribe, I asked them if anyone wanted to travel with me. They gave me another donkey. Now I had two loyal friends to scream at me in demonic voices.

I welcomed him aboard, read a strange scroll I had purchased from a shaman, and accidentally turned him into a hulking, cannibalistic monstrosity. The creature turned out to be remarkably polite and well-behaved, though he did eat one of my beloved donkeys. It's just as well, given that I later killed and devoured the monster in a fit of karmic irony. In the end, I ate my last remaining donkey and died of starvation while trying to flee from a gigantic crab that I had angered by entering its territory.
10/10, would cannibalize again.

Gameplay
Each faction has its own units and bonuses which help diversify each game. For example the roving clan can’t declare war on any faction and can block others from the market.
The gameplay, with the exception of the combat, is well handled. Everything is clearly set up and easy to find, such as the market screen or the hero screen and the upgrade screen is very good as well so credit where credit is due.
On the hole, I say that the combat is the weakest part of the game. When you enter a battle, say a broken lord’s army against an army of demons, the gameplay descends into setup you’re units pick if they hold positions, be defensive or aggressive then select start. Each battle has 6 phases after the sixth phase the battle ends and you return to the world map. All of this is fine, but were the game falls down is that apart from what has been stated above you control very little. It’s not the worsted I have seen, but the combat is very uninvolving and giving your orders in-between phases in a nightmare. For example say you want to pull a unit back because a better unit can take its place, well if that unit is attacked the order will not be followed. This makes coordinating your army mid battle very hard and it is very irritating when your best unit is killed because before they could pull back the enemy rudely attacked you before they could move and for some reason your unit decides to stay where it is and die.
Story
Each faction has its own story and quest, which I will not spoil, and each one gives the player reasons to explore and perform certain tasks. The timed quests are however really irritating. The problem is that the timed quests do not change or adapted in anyway. For example I got one quest were I had to complete by the end of the winter however I clicked next turn and winter had ended and I failed the quest. The developers do need to fix this because it is highly unfair to the player.
Graphics/Astatic
The graphics are okay, it’s the astatic and design that are really interesting. Each faction is very well designed and the weapons and armour looks brilliant. The landscape in the game is excellent and well-made and the animations are also well done. All and all the animations, Graphics and Astatic are very good and handled with care.

Not only is this a fantastic game, an instant 10/10, the fact that it costs only £2 makes it one of the best value-for-money games I've ever seen on Steam, at least not including sales. It took me 20 hours to complete this game, so that's £1 per 10 hours.
The game itself is a classic, growing on what made Abe's Oddysee so great, and while I think Exoddus lacks the atmosphere that made the original so enjoyable, the gameplay itself is much more varied (though I still prefer Oddysee). The cutscenes are better, the music is more complex (if not a tad generic), there are more places and environments to see, and there are more types of puzzles based on the emotion system with the Mudokons. They can be angry, depressed, wired (in other words happy), sick, and blind. This means a lot more is explored as to how the Mudokons interact with you, and especially trying to handle the wired Mudokons running about with enemies, bombs and motion sensors around can get very tense.
You can also autosave, another improvement from Oddysee that makes the game much less frustrating.
I have 2 complaints, however; the first being there are a few ridiculous chase sections that force you to duck and react quickly with a movement system not internded for fast-paced action, rather slow-moving stealth. The game also overstays it's welcome a bit, getting dragged out for a few more hours than it really needed to last.
Speaking of stealth, once again every single enemy can make your palms sweat all over your controller, especially if you have some blind Mudokons you have to escort.
One more thing; the graphics, for 1998, are amazing. I found myself stopping and gazing at some of the fantastically detailed backdrops of places like Necrum and the Soulstorm Brewery. It's dark and beautifully rendered.
Anyway, get the game now. It's bloody great.

Kings of Strategy, Paradox Interactive's late modern era game. Historical events and options are plentiful. A shorter timespan than most PI games, only 100 years, from 1836 to 1936, as opposed to the four centuries that Crusader Kings and Europa Universalis have. Starting just at the rise of Pax Britannica, just after the falls of the French and Spanish Empires, there's so much to do in this game. Form the German Empire. Try and stay an Absolute Monarchy through the rise of Liberalism, Socialism, Communism and Fascism. Act out America's Manifest Destiny and partake in the Civil War. Play the Chinese Empire and try and modernise and resist foreign influences. Play the Ottoman Empire and prevent your backslide into historical obscurity. There's so much to do, and you've got to make your own goals. In usual Paradox style there's a ton of super-complex systems that you need to know, but if you get a handle on it, there's so much depth and replayabilitiy to be done.

The HD graphics upgrade compared to the tiny resolution of the PSP is a big plus as well.
Although there is some minor quality fluctuations (the blue swirly background at the beginning has artifacts leftover from upscaling for example) in this HD localised port, it's of little importance compared to the gloriousness of HD beautiful boys and sexy Japanese voice acting that they kept.
Drool away, ladies, and don't forget to find the numerous drama CDs and character songs if you can understand Japanese (and also the three to four spinoffs in this series that they haven't translated).

Would I recommend this game? Yes, moreso than damn near any other game I have on steam. Why? Well, for one, it's free, so if you hate it you're out nothing but some bandwidth to download the game and a few minutes of your time. If, like myself, you love it, congrats, you're still out nothing.
Why do I love this game so much? Great question. The bizarrely titled "Only If" is one of the few, very few videogames I've ever played to truely get an actual, thought provoking reaction out of me. The game made me think. Not through the use of being boring, plodding, pretentious like so many other walking simulators out there try and fail to do. No, this game got a reaction out of me in much the same way that a book like Blood Meridian or something along those lines gets a reaction out of you: it takes the sledgehammer to the face approach of getting your attention. It flat out up and screams at you, look, this is what you should think about. Think about it, okay? And you know what? For me, at least, it worked.
Take the same kind of vibe Guy Ritchie's film Revolver has going, an opening that reminded me a bit of the game Manhunt in its "hide or you will be gunned down like a rabid dog" vibe.  Take a few of the better-done pop-culture references I've ever seen in a videogame, some actually really quite good voice acting from all parties involved, and a seriously good score that flip flops between funky and beautiful, and you've kinda sorta not really got a game like Only If. I've never really seen much like it.
It has its glitches, yes, though it ran flawlessly on my toaster of a computer. Subtitles would be nice, and the ending slams you in the face with its silliness. But this bad boy's about the journey, not the destination. And what a journey it is.
Consult the guide if you decide to play this and get stuck. There's a very well written one on steam that clears up a few of the murkier objectives in the game. Much easier than ragequitting and the game's final levels really are stunning.
If you are, as many of the so-called professional gaming journalists are, offended easily, do not play this game, however. It has very coarse language in it, exactly like the store page flat out warns you about before you download it.
If you have not reached the level of maturity to be able to handle a pair of fictional characters using foul language and a slur or two in a work of fiction that is in no way, shape, or form inspired by real events... You should steer clear of this game. If the british slang term for a cigarette being used as an insult by a fictional teenage frat boy to describe a man that's tried to kill him on several occasions strikes you as something your delicate ears cannot bear hearing... Do not play this game.
However. If you think you can handle it, and want something so, so different... Buy the ticket, take the ride. Difference being that this bad boy's ticket's free, and it's hard to beat a ride this good for a ticket that cheap.
Oh, and pick the black pawn first.

A great entertaining game!
It is still in alpha (11 as I'm writing this) but already very enjoyable and quit addictive.
You play a 19th century explorer heading out to six expeditions in a row to find the golden pyramid at the end of each expedition. On the way you loot and collect treasure, fight wild animals, natives or monsters and haggle with traders, natives or monsters... I mean slave traders. Between the expeditions treasure can be given to the museum for fame or sold to gain money for buying equipment for your next expedition.
An overview:
+ great atmosphere (you just have to love that nice retro pixel graphics)
+ dice roll combat system that is very fun with lots of dice combinations
+ surprising and fun events (transforming a jungle into a desert by accident or witnessing how one of your expedition members suddenly transforms into... something else)
+ recruit, dismiss and level your expedition members
+ management of items vs treasure, what to keep, what to toss?
+ great replay value because of many characters to choose from and random expeditions
+ great for playing in between, early expeditions take 5 to 10 minutes, later ones up to 30 minutes
Still in alpha, so the following issues will hopefully be addressed or fixed:
- many events are often very similar. A bit more diversity of hints and events would be nice
- very many texts and sometimes you click too fast and can't go back
- no chance to let time go on without moving (when trapped by rising water on one tile you can't do anything because time does not go on)
- you can only save between expeditions
- you can't sell or discard mundane items between missions
- too few combat combo opitions for the blue face dice
- sometimes the balance and difficulty in later missions is very frustrating (but developers promised to focus on this in the next patch)
- no record of your previous successes (or to be more accurate: failures)
- not much content when finishing the game (I believe a statue was mentioned?)
I have tons of fun playing this game and after 11 tries and 15 hours playtime I even managed to finish my sixth expedition, coming first, which was not so difficult, but surviving that's the hard part ^^'

This game is pretty fun. While overall, there are a few balance issues (some combinations of Nauts, the different characters you can play as, are near impossible to beat, while other combinations are just flat terrible and can't win, or only win a small percentage of games- I don't feel this should happen in a really well-balanced game) the game does have a lot of charm.
However, this is a game of strategy and it seems not too many players fully understand that. If you play online, players in the lower leagues will be atrocious, only shooting for kills. You need to make friends with the good players you meet before trying to get too far ahead, as randoms will leave you frustrated. Also, unfortunately, the better you get, the worse the community seems to get.  If you're set on playing this game online, be prepared to meet people who will degrade you in every form possible (curse words, blaming long before the game is won/lost, being told to uninstall) if you make the slightest slip-up. Being able to chat with the enemy team only adds to how much of this you'll see, as the enemies will post that you suck, it's clear they're gonna win, etc. The only real nice thing about the community is the half-hearted 'gg's at the end of every match.
Another problem with online - The game utilizes peer to peer connections. In other words, be prepared to experience anywhere from slight to game-crippling lag every other match. Sometimes your character will freeze and show a big 'Reconnecting' sign. Pray this happens in a safe place because you can still be attacked and killed in this state and enemies are very quick to jump the gun on a defenseless character with bad connection (another community charm). From the looks of it, the developers have no plans of doing anything to resolve this issue - they are set on peer to peer and from the looks of it, don't have plans on making a reconnecting character invincible or un-interactable. So, if you get this game, be prepared to see this kind of stuff for as long as you should choose to play it.
Basically, if you want a game with a lot of charm, a really interesting variety of characters, and fast paced MOBA/Platformer style fun, Awesomenauts is the game for you. If you like a perfectly balanced game with a competitive, yet respectful community and no serious network issues effectively coded into the core of the game... save yourself!
EDIT: This game has gotten progressively worse since my initial review. Community is worse and as small as it was months ago despite a $1.00 sale, Ronimo constantly adds but never fixes, and this game is a shell of what it once was. Highly do not recommend this game anymore. It's just atrocious, what it has become.

A well made fantasy version of Endless Space, almost like a mod because it uses the same hero system. The game is also worth trying if you enjoyed Stardock's Fallen Enchantress series, Civilization, or Warlock.
Each race has their own victory quest storyline you can follow. Heroes can manage cities or armies. Game has market system to be able to puchase luxuries or strategic resources if you got the shaft by the random map maker. The market also has heroes and units for sale you would not be able to build yourself.
The tactical combats are only six turns long which can be used to hold out for an escape or it could take multiple turns to wipe multiple armies out. Multiple armies can be involved in a tactical combat depending on their distance and anything past the initial target and targer has to arrive a few units at a time via a reinforcement system.
If you enjoyed the one city challenge in Civilization IV then this game is fairly balanced to do the same. This is because luxury buffs, research costs, and empire plans costs are dependant on how many cities you own,
Lots of interesting spins on the 4X genre. Plays like Civ, but a little more complex and a lot more beautiful.

A great walking simulator with an excellent story well told.  Unfortunately, as the development studio are from the USA there is a fair amount of fiddle-dee-dee-isation going on.  The voice acting, while competently done, was wholly unsuitable for people who are supposed to be from Belfast.  And there are other representations of life in the north of the island which are predictably twee.  Regardless, it's still a well told story.  And the gameplay is solid as well, as there's a fair amount of interaction to keep the walking simulator experience from growing stale.  At first it has you running from heat source to heat source to stave off hypothermia, and then you're redirecting steam to clear off swarming insects or put out fires, or draining pools to open up new areas. Most walking simulators showcase landscapes with forests and meadows. Fidelio, on the other hand, takes us close to Iceland where Stanley must survive following the crash of his plane. While he is desperate to find shelter he also needs to think of the other passenger, his wife, Leonore, who also managed to stay alive. During our journey we need to press forward towards the inland and occasionally need to find some objects and turn some levers in the relevant order.
This game looks gorgeous. For me the most captivating were the scenes taking place in the icy caves (albeit there were few and they were rather short) and sections throughout the forest that is on fire. Stanley regularly receives a call from his wife (too bad this is only a one-way communication) who orders him that all their documents be collected so that nothing is left behind for unwanted eyes. It is unfortunate that of all the achievements this one in particular is bugged and even after collecting all 30 items this was not granted to me.
The accompanying music is great and is freely available as an extra downloadable content. Stanley's story is quite emotional; emotional not only because it is a journey of survival and of finding your loved ones but it is moving as by collecting all pages you'll soon learn this man's very past he wants to forget. I rarely complete walking sims twice in quick succession but this game, incidentally, opens up that list.

This has got to be one of my most favorite games in my Steam Library but trying to adequately describe it is a bit hard. The best description I can come up with is that of a card-based, tabletop (in a simular vein to that of Monoply) multiplayer battle game in which the roll of the dice and careful use of a card can easily lead to situations of Triumphant victory, Crushing defeat,  Hard-fought battles, or confusingly hilarious messes in which there are no real winners. If you lile Mario Party than this game may be just what you are looking for.
100% Orange Juice is balanced in such a way that even if you play a character or have cards at your disposal that may grant you an advantage (like say survival in a fight) these is still this foreboding sense that your plan can (an probably will) go wrong. The game is impartial, it will be mean to everyone regardless of strategy (or lack there of) so it is perfectly fair (even if it doesn't feel that way all the time, lol). However, those advantages that a certain character (or card) grant also do have an effect on the game and how the game should be played for each player. Whether you deside to play aggressively, passively, strategically, playing as an opportunist, playing as a pacifist, attempting to mess up everyone else's day, or living the YOLO life this game is somthing you should try.
As frustrating as I may make this sound winning an losing a game can be its own reward here. I've had a few come from behind victories and "EXODIA" moments in matches when everything lines up into a perfect storm of awesome and it is so satisfying.  I've also had some matches where I esentually go nowhere, do nothing, have victory narrowly stolen from my grasp, have no effect on the match at all, or get used as someone elses footstool to victory. That is the nature of 100% Orange Juice though, not everything's going to go your way........but it might and sometimes giving your all with everyone else can be super fun, Win or Lose.

Crusader Kings 2 is a grand strategy game made by the masters of the genre, Paradox Interactive. You play as a ruler of your choosing, or a ruler that you created yourself, if you purchased the Ruler Designer DLC (facepalm). The start dates spans from the fall of the Western Roman Empire to the High Middle Ages, the game ends itself once you reach the mid 15th century. From there you can transfer your game save into Europa Universalis IV, if you purchased the Converter DLC (facepalm).
The game is updated regularly, even after almost 6 years, and has regular expansions released, however, I must say that as of late the expansions are growing stale. With all of the games expansions, and even withouth them, the game becomes incredibly complex, with tons of interesting systems, from cults, epidemics, silk road, crusades, jihads, and even a sunset invasion from the new world (facepalm). Much of this content is worthy of being in a expansion, but much of it is not, and should have been a part of a regular content update. In regards to cosmetics, I understand that the developers need to make money in order to keep the game updated, but it does come off as being nickel and dimed. Thankfully they have condensed the old cosmetic packs into a single dlc, and all future cosmetic dlc is included in the expansion.
If you enjoy politics, military tactics, and occasional incest or pedophilia, Crusader Kings 2 is the game for you. All jokes aside, the game understands the culture of its time, which definitely makes situations in the game, such as being 80 years old and marrying your 16 year old cousin, terribly awkward. Its not really a bad thing, but no Crusader Kings 2 review is complete without a incest joke. Waging war in the game is often about who has the most manpower, just like in real life, however, you can find yourself defeating a overwhelming force, if you apply real world tactics, such as naturally defensible positions, or use very talented generals. The games political system is ever so complex that I simply reccomend reading The Prince by Niccolo Machiavelli in order to grasp it. Im exaggerating, but assassinations, political mishaps, affairs, espionage, etc., is all in common place in this game.
Overrall, I highly reccomend Crusader Kings 2 for lovers of history and alternate history, and I also reccomend it as someone's first Grand Strategy game. Try and pick this one up while its on sale, along with its expansions, and you will be dumping hundreds of hours into it in no time. I reccomend having a friend to explain the game to you or watching lots of tutorials and gameplay. This game does take awhile to learn, but not much longer to master.
Enjoy!

One of the most annoying games I've played in a while.  It should have been something amazing, but utter failed to be anything close to that.
My biggest complaint is that the game simply makes no sense.  It's claimed to be a "surreal" puzzle game; but as so often happens, "surreal" means little more than "random stuff stuck together".  A truly surreal atmosphere should have an internal logic that can be discovered and deciphered.  Some type of coherent theme underlying the seeming chaos.  As others have noted, there is no logic, surreal or otherwise, to this game.  No method to the madness.  Not to the story, what little there is; and certainly not to the mechanics.
The gameplay starts out as a bog-standard point-and-click adventure - pick things up in one location, then put them down in another - but then drops in a text-entry mechanic without the slightest hint that it even exists, let alone how to use it or what the game is expecting.  Eventually I discovered it with the aid of a walkthrough for the first instance, and managed to figure out out well enough when I encountered it again.  And when I am finally starting to enjoy it, it discards that mechanic and throws in a jumping puzzle.  Wait what?  Even more irritatingly, it then transformed into a platformer; at which point I simply gave up.  (The fact that I loathe platformers did not help one bit).
And what was that "millenial" reference about?  And the Inception reference?  Why was that even in there?  And the rest of the dialog, the commentary on self-sacrifice?  What is that about?  It's like the developer is trying to shore up a poorly written game by using pop culture references and pretentious dialog to make it sounds more "deep" and "relevant" than it ever manages to be.
The game is pertty, I'll give it that.  The voice acting, on the other hand, was irritating.  The main character was wooden at best, but at least I could hear him.  The other character voices are actually quite decently done; but faded in and out badly, and were too easy to lose track of.
It feels like the developer had a good idea for a game; then didn't quite know what to do with it.  There's a gem of originality here; buried under the pile of same-old-same-old game mechanics and tropes.  I do hope that the gem will eventually shine through in a new game, because it's not terribly visible here.

Amnesia™: Memories is an interesting and addicting adventure. You follow the main character on her quest to retrieve her memories. In order to do that, she visits 4 different worlds (1 you unlock later) each with different distinct story line. However, in each world you have a different man as the main characters boyfriend. As you play you have to make different choices that in the end, affect the outcome of your story. It is truely a beautifully written game.
You grow to love all the different guys and you get addicted to their story line. "Just 5 more minutes!" you keep saying to yourself but you find yourself unable to pull yourself away. Each guy is different and unique in their own way. My personal favorite has to be Kent, though Shin is right behind him. Both have an amazing story line. Ikki's story line is fun but you (as well as the main character) feel the frustration. I was very worried about Toma's story line and I would have to say it probably my least favorite. As for Ukyo's, I actually enjoyed his story line and it had one hell of an ending. Overall, I loved the unique story lines and it really pulled me in. I have only gotten the good endings and I look forward to getting the other ones as well.
They also made an anime which is very beautiful and I would recommend watching after you play through the story lines if you really love the game and wanna see it animated!

I cannot recommend this game.  This game reminds me of a slot machine.  While it technically requires your input, it is almost entirely luck based.  And like playing the lottery, your chances of winning are extremely slim.  Perhaps the game’s one true quality is that, like a slot machine, it is very addictive.  Every time you lose, you feel the urge to play the game again; hoping this time you’ll have better luck.  And luck is what it’s all about.  There is a dice role behind almost every facet of this game.  Who will you have the opportunity to recruit?  Will you get swallowed up in growing pit as you try to run away?  Will you randomly walk towards the temple, or will it be placed in the most remote region of the map?  The game is not entirely luck, however luck plays an overwhelming role in your success or failure.  There are some choices you can make which are clearly better than others.  For example, an abomination is a great addition to your party.  However, you have to be lucky enough to stumble upon a scroll of abomination before you have the opportunity to make that decision.  If you are lucky enough to recruit a strong party, you might choose to attack animals as a way to make money.
Combat is this game’s one strength.  Like a game of poker, the combat combines strategy with elements of luck.  Unfortunately, strategy does not play a significant role in other aspects of the game.  You can make all the best decisions and still lose over and over again.
